Louise Mushikiwabo a Rwandan national currently serving her second term at the La Francophonie organisation is seeking a third term and may most likely grab it.

L’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) is scheduled to hold elections for it’s new leader On November 16, in Phnom Penh.

Candidates include; Rwandan Louise Mushikiwabo, Congolese Juliana Amato Lumumba, Mauritanian Coumba Bâ, and Romanian Dacian Cioloș, however the wrestle for the seat has sucked in the rivalry between Rwanda and DRC.

Ever since Mushikiwabo won the OIF seat in 2018, Kinshasa has never taken it lightly and subsequently refused Mushikiwabo on their soil even when DRC hosted La Francophonie games in August 2023.

Despite the ongoing military campaign in the Eastern part of the Democratic Republic of Congo between the government troops and the FRN rebels movement Kinshasa continues to accuse Kigali of aiding the rebels an accusation vehemently rejected by Kigali.

Kigali has in response accused the Kinshasa regime of providing cover to FDLR rebels designated by Washington as a terrorist organisation.

Most members of the FDLR are perpetrators of the 1994 genocide against Tutsi in Rwanda which claimed a million lives.

Kinshasa believes that by fielding a candidate in the challenge for OIF’s new leader it is a war against Rwanda.

Mushikiwabo has the advantage of incumbency since her election in 2018 and reelected in 2022.

She has mastered decision-making mechanisms, and the internal balances of the organization.

She can defend the continuity of her actions based on a record that members have observed over two terms.

The precedent of Abdou Diouf, who led the Francophonie for three terms, shows that another reelection is possible.

After eight years at the helm of the OIF, that same record may lead some members to favor stability, and others to seek new priorities.

“Mushikiwabo has all the skills for the job– so I will back her,” French President Emmanuel Macron said in 2018.

“There is a tremendous converge of economic and geopolitical interests behind Mushikiwabo’s candidacy,” Pascal Airault, a journalist at French weekly “L’Opinion” and co-author of “Françafrique.

Rwandan leader Paul Kagame has actively lobbied African leaders and OIF member states to secure Mushikiwabo’s election.

Kinshasa has fielded Juliana Amato Lumumba as candidate for OIF top job .

The Tshisekedi camp seeks to convert the demographic weight of the DRC into institutional influence.

Amato Lumumba’s candidacy raises a question: what place does the Francophonie give, in its leadership and programs, to one of its main demographic and cultural hubs?

This argument can give her a hearing beyond Kinshasa’s partners.

Her challenge will be to convince delegations favorable to alternation but reluctant to see the next leadership dominated by tensions between the two capitals.

The more her candidacy is seen as a way to rebuke Kigali, the harder it will be for her to rally support around her own project.

MN202611_3uhzjiaw0c.t:
The angling club said that the pollution incident killed brown and migratory sea trout

A investigation is underway after "a major fish kill" in a County Down river, the Department for Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera) has confirmed.

The pollution caused the death of brown and migratory sea trout in the Gransha, Ballystockart and Inler (also known as Enler) Rivers.

Glenn McKibbin, the secretary of Inler Angling Club, said about 1,000 fish were killed in the incident and it "could not have happened in a worse location on the river or at a worse time".

The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) and Daera Inland Fisheries are working to "identify the source of the pollution and to finalise the numbers of fish killed".

The Department said the incident was reported by a member of the public on Tuesday at 09:30 GMT.

The club said that the fish killing impacts resident kingfishers, herons and otters

McKibbin said that "current and future fish stocks obliterated for years to come".

He added that resident and non-resident migratory fish, which only return at this of year to spawn, have been impacted.

"Knock-on effects for other wildlife such as resident kingfishers, herons & otters unavoidable.

"For our members and volunteers who work tirelessly in a bid to improve the river this is soul-destroying, particularly as the river was still in recovery from major pollution incidents / fish kills in 2013 and 2015," McKibbin said.

"Waterways up and down the country continue to be treated like sewers.

"The paltry fines that usually follow incidents of this nature are not a deterrent and the current 'system' is broken."

Many migratory fish, such as trout and salmon, swim up smaller tributaries to lay their eggs in cleaner, gravel-bottomed, or cooler waters away from larger predators in the main river.

A tributary is a smaller river that flows into a larger mainstem river where many migratory fish, such as trout and salmon, swim up to lay their eggs away from larger predators in the main river.

Inler Angling Club Chairperson David Pyper said: "For those who dedicate so much time and effort to caring for the river, witnessing the sheer loss of fish in circumstances such as these is particularly disappointing.

"The club hopes that the forthcoming investigations will establish the cause of this latest incident and help ensure appropriate steps are taken to protect the river and its wildlife."

The club has encouraged local representatives and authorities to continue to prioritise rivers and direct resources towards improving water quality and preventing further incidents.

MN202611_14vje2xbbhj.t:
England captain Harry Kane scored scored 213 times in 320 league games for Tottenham

Harry Kane's decision to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich carries heavy significance for the Bundesliga giants, who have been celebrating his status as a Ballon d'Or winner, but also for England and the Premier League's record books.

Bayern have acted swiftly to secure the 33-year-old on a deal taking him through to 2029 after he was crowned the world's best player, ensuring England's captain and record goalscorer will spend the final peak years of a magnificent career at Allianz Arena.

Kane has written himself into Bayern legend since joining from Spurs for £86m in August 2023, scoring 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches, winning two league titles and three successive Golden Boot awards.

It is why Bayern could not contemplate his departure as other clubs eyed his next move - and why the announcement Kane is staying casts ripples far beyond Munich.

Does it mean Kane will never grace the Premier League again? And does it mean - far more enticingly - he has his sights set on two more major tournaments and two more chances to grasp the prize that has eluded him at international level?

Former England striker Chris Sutton told BBC Sport: "I certainly think, although you always have to factor fitness issues into all of this, that Harry is more than capable of carrying on for a few years yet, easily.

"People might say his game lacks a little bit of pace, but he's so strong in other areas. He is a world-class all-round player. His finishing isn't going to be affected in any way by his age. He can still link up play and his football brain is first class.

"I don't see his age being such a big deal. You think of pacy players over the years who rely on that part of the game then lose it as they get older. Harry is not one of those. He seems fit and at the peak of his powers with Bayern and England."

Kane's new contract expires shortly before his 36th birthday, certainly raising the prospect the player who left Spurs as the highest scorer in their history with 280 goals in 435 appearances may never grace the Premier League again.

His consummate professionalism, and apparent ability to develop into the complete player with age, means this can never be discounted.

The notion of an emotional return to Spurs at some point has often provided background noise, but now looks increasingly unlikely.

What it surely means is that Alan Shearer will remain the Premier League's highest scorer - who knows what will happen with Erling Haaland as Manchester City await punishment after being found guilty of breaching financial regulations they deny? - and out of Kane's reach.

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or after 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025–26 season

Shearer scored 260 goals in 441 Premier League matches for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United. Kane scored 213 times in 320 league games for Spurs.

With Kane still 47 short of Shearer's record, it would need a spectacular late-career flourish for him to eclipse the Geordie icon's tally to write another entry into the history books, which also have him as England's highest scorer with 91 goals from a record-equalling 125 caps.

What will be of huge interest to Thomas Tuchel - the coach who took him to Bayern and now leads England - is that Kane has delivered a clear indication that Euro 2028, to be played in the UK and Ireland, is firmly in his sights.

And, when this new deal expires, Kane is also only a year away from the 2030 World Cup, to be played in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, with special centenary opening matches held in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay.

This, of course, is a stretch given the inevitable rigours of age, but few who know Kane, who have watched him move to a new level at Bayern, would ever say never to such a driven personality, hiding fierce mental strength and a competitive instinct behind his humble 'anti-superstar' persona.

Sutton said: "Euro 2028 certainly shouldn't be a problem and who knows beyond that? If Harry has got players around him with pace and dynamism, as well as runners in and around him, then his football brain isn't going to change and he can still play a huge part.

"He's such a sharp, quick, thinker. He reads the game superbly, knows where his next pass is going and has shown an ability to drop deep and impact the game.

"Harry just seems to be getting better and more rounded with age. And as for age, just look at someone like Teddy Sheringham. He was playing and scoring goals for West Ham United in the Premier League in his 40s.

"Sheringham was an incredibly talented player with supreme intelligence. Harry Kane falls right into the same category.

"Ronaldo has just retired from international football with Portugal at 41, but he is a totally different player than Harry Kane. Harry is one who can drop a little bit deeper to use his incredible ability and range of passing.

"As well as that ability, it is about how Harry's football brain works as much as anything and that won't change with age."

'My heart was beating so fast' - Kane wins Ballon D'or

And it is an argument, and a hope, that is even more pertinent as England still do not possess any other striker or forward who could be considered anywhere near Kane's class or potency.

"When you talk about 2028 or 2030, who are the English strikers coming through to challenge him to take him out of the team?" said Sutton. "There's no-one in his class or effectiveness, or anywhere near it."

What also plays into the argument that Kane cannot be ruled out of such long-term involvement is the manner in which he responded so superbly to what was a disappointing Euro 2024, not only as England lost in the final to Spain but because he looked a jaded shadow of his old self.

Kane looked so out of sorts there was a clamour for him to be replaced by Ollie Watkins, then at Aston Villa. He was substituted in all of England's knockout matches, including after only 61 minutes of that final loss to Spain in Berlin.

And yet, Kane still finished as the tournament's joint top scorer with three goals from seven games.

The notion of him being replaced with the stakes so high now is unthinkable, such is his peerless form and stature.

While Bayern are convinced their new investment in Kane's brilliance will be rewarded with further honours, Tuchel will hope it is motivation and inspiration to finally end the country's long wait for international glory.

MN202611_lko7u7h4b1.t:
Brand's stillness was striking in the dock

This was not the Russell Brand most people will remember from the height of his noughties TV and comedy fame.

The flamboyant character with big gestures and provocative one-liners was not the man we saw in the courtroom.

During his rape trial, Brand mostly sat impassively in the dock, staring straight ahead. His stillness was striking. His face betrayed no visible emotion or reaction as the string of allegations against him were outlined in detail over several days.

After a three-week trial, the 51-year-old was found guilty of one charge of rape and three charges of sexual assault. He was found not guilty of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The allegations spanned a 10-year period from 1999 to 2009 and involved six female complainants.

More women likely to come forward, says detective who led Russell Brand investigation

Russell Brand found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault

The Brand on show in this trial seemed courteous to a fault.

Yet the polite, respectful man we saw holding doors open and thanking court staff was in striking contrast to the evidence we heard.

His victims told of a brash, arrogant, sexually voracious man who did not take no for an answer from the women he preyed on; a ruthless rapist and manipulative sex offender.

Flashes of the Brand we were used to seeing in the media were not totally absent - they often manifested themselves in the morning when he would arrive at Southwark Crown Court.

Mostly dressed in variations of dark jackets and trousers, long scarves and open-neck shirts, he would often make a beeline for the media scrum outside the courthouse.

Watch: Russell Brand addresses the media as he arrives at court on the first day of his trial

On day one of the trial, he confidently uttered the words: "Today, I feel blessed. I feel of course concerned, but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved. That's my prayer."

In all my years of covering court cases I've never seen a defendant address journalists during a trial. His professed hatred for the mainstream media clearly did not stop him from having his say.

Sitting on the floor of a court corridor in the early days of the trial, I was tapping on my phone when Brand walked past.

"Hello, mate!" came his cheery greeting. It was a bizarre moment given the seriousness of his situation. I continued typing.

In another slightly surreal moment a black people carrier pulled up outside the court on the day the trial began.

Some reporters did a double-take when a man looking a little like Brand showed up outside the court

The door to the car slid open and out stepped a man who looked just like Brand - but it wasn't him.

The mystery man attracted a few shouted questions before Brand stepped out of the car behind him.

The man was present on most days of the trial and wandered around after Brand, attracting double-takes and much comment, with no clarity about who he actually was.

Brand now positions himself as a Christian influencer and has been public about his faith. It was on display during his trial via the crucifixes of varying sizes that he wore. One day, I saw him handling what looked like prayer beads.

The court room itself was typical. The judge faced Brand, who sat in a long glass box with a door at one end, which was mostly left open, giving him a view of his wife.

I was directly behind him - no more than a metre and a half away in the press seats. Between Brand and the judge, sat two sets of lawyers with the jury sitting immediately to the right of the judge.

Day after day we listened to harrowing and graphic accounts of rape and sexual abuse by Brand, some of the worst kinds imaginable.

The courage of the women who told their stories in court, who spoke behind a screen, was remarkable. The tears flowed, their nerves evident in their voices. The way they told their stories was deeply moving.

In the dock Brand's statue-like demeanour was broken only occasionally, when, during some of the evidence, he closed his eyes for several seconds, perhaps in silent prayer or meditation. There was no fidgeting or movement. He didn't flinch.

He maintained his composure even during some of the most harrowing evidence, when one of the victims told the court how blood and faeces had been left on Brand's bed sheets after he had raped her at his house.

During the testimony, Brand let out a sigh and looked at the ceiling with his eyes closed.

Speculation grew about whether Brand would give evidence - defendants can choose whether to take to the stand in their trials. It became a daily talking point among the reporters.

Giving evidence yourself can be a double-edged sword; a chance to vigorously defend one's innocence on the one hand, balanced by the risk of being torn apart by the prosecution barrister.

But it finally happened. Brand took to the witness box on day 10 of the trial. His testimony was perhaps unsurprising - after all, nobody apart from his wife had been prepared to speak up for him in court as part of the defence's case.

Brand entered the witness box wearing a dark suit and a white open-necked shirt. It was a nervous beginning. In an unusually loud voice he answered "no" to each of the allegations that were put to him.

He had taken his bible oath loudly too and stood, bolt upright with hands clasped behind his back.

I watched him like a hawk. This was a TV personality who was very much part of my youth, but now being interrogated with his liberty on the line.

His nerves seemed to visibly ease, so much so that at one point he put his hands in his pockets. It was noticeable that after an adjournment, he was back in his ramrod style stance with hands out of his pockets, behind his back.

The trial had hinged on the issue of consent. During his testimony Brand stated that "consent is fundamental, essential, necessary and indeed in many ways more important than sex itself".

But many of his answers were terse, followed sometimes by silences. This led the prosecution to suggest it had been because he was finding the questions difficult to answer.

There were flashes of irritability. "Do you accept you were desperate for it [sex] and sometimes couldn't function without it?" he was asked. "No", he replied, displaying an apparent frustration at the repetitive nature of the questioning.

There were moments of bizarre levity too. When his wife, Laura, gave evidence in his defence, he laughed out loud from the dock when she spoke about them having plenty of friends and being grateful for them. It was the only moment throughout the trial where Brand had shown any visible emotion.

Brand's wife Laura was supported by her father Bernard Gallacher who sat next to her in the gallery

His wife attended court with him every day - soberly dressed, she sometimes took notes when the complainants were giving evidence.

Her support for her husband was visible - holding his hand as they walked in, smiling at him while he was in the dock for hours at a time.

Brand's minder often sat next to her in the public benches, and her father, former Ryder Cup-winning golfer Bernard Gallacher sat with her in the gallery during the defence closing. Brand's father, Ron, also attended regularly, exchanging polite chat with some of the media.

At 51 years of age, Brand looked gaunt and visibly thinner as the trial neared its end, he seemed to have lost weight as the days went on. Other reporters said the same. We discussed whether signs of confidence he showed at the start had slowly ebbed away.

The verdicts came on Thursday after the jury had been deliberating for eight hours and 30 minutes.

Brand, who stood upright in the dock, showed limited emotion as the verdicts were read out. "Sit down Mr Brand," the judge told him after the verdicts were delivered.

"On what happens next," he added, "obviously a custodial sentence of some length will result."

Brand mouthed "I'm good, I'm good" to his defence counsel as he was led away.

But his appearance in court was an extraordinary fall from grace. A man hailed as a multi-media celebrity, a self-confessed ladies' man too, but now a convicted rapist in custody.

You can follow analysis and further insights on the BBC podcast Russell Brand on Trial - available on BBC Sounds, YouTube, iPlayer, or wherever you get your BBC podcasts

Buri mwaka ku wa 31 Ukwakira, ku Isi hizihizwa umunsi mpuzamahanga wahariwe kuzigama, uyu mwaka ukaba warizihijwe ku nshuro ya 37.

Mu Rwanda wizihirijwe mu Karere ka Kayonza kuri uyu wa Kane, ku nsanganyamatsiko igira iti "Kuzigama, Umusingi w'Iterambere."

Abatuye muri ako Karere bamaze gukengerwa n'umuco wo kwizigamira bagaragaza ko byabafashije kwiteza imbere kuko hari aho byabakuye n'aho bimaze kubageza.

Ati "Twatangiye dufite igishoro nabara ko kiri muri miliyoni 5, noneho tuyoboka ibigo by'imari, dutangira kuzigama, tuza gusaba inguzanyo, bwa mbere baduhaha iya miliyoni 8, bitewe n'uko twari dutangiye kugenda tuzamuka, tuza gusaba iya kabiri baduha milyoni 16. Ubu navuga ko birimo biragenda neza kuko korora, turorora, tugakora n'ibiryo by'amatungo kandi dukoresheje iby'iwacu bidahenze cyane."

Ku rundi ruhande ariko hari abavuga ko kuba izuba ryaravuye igihe kirekire, bikagira ingaruka ku izamuka ry'ibiciro ku isoko, byatumye ayo bazigamaga hari abo agabanuka, abandi barayabura kubera ko bahisemo kuyakoresha muri gahunda zo gutunga umuryango.

Deborah Nyirahabimana wo mu Murenge wa Gahini, ni umwe mu bazigama bakoresheje ibimina, uvuga ko ayo yazigamaga yagabanutse.

Ati "Ntabwo byoroshye kubera ko umusaruro wo muri sizoni ishize wabaye muke, no kwizigamira byabaye bike. Mbere nazigamaga 2,000 mu cyemweru ariko ubu hari igihe mbona 500, hari n'igihe nyabura nkararanya."

Umuyobozi Mukuru ushinzwe amabanki n’ibigo by’imari bitari amabanki muri MINECOFIN, Cyllile Hategekimana, avuga ko ubwizigame bw'Abanyarwanda burimo kugenda butera imbere cyane, kuko abenshi bitabira gahunda y'ibimina na za SACCO.

Ati " Iyo urebye ukuntu Abanyarwanda bitabira izo gahunda ndetse na gahunda ya Ejo Heza, bikwereka ko Abanyarwanda bose serivisi z'imari zagiye zibegerezwa kandi bagenda bazigana. Ikibigaragaza cyane nk'ubwizigame bw'ibimina dufite uyu munsi, ibyo tumaze kwandika muri MINECOFIN, bigera hejuru y'ibihumbi 15, bifite ubwizigame bumaze kugera kuri miliyali 54 Frw, ayo mafaranga aturuka muri abo baturage bari hirya no hino."

Imirenge SACCO yo iganwa n'abaturage barenga miliyoni 4.4, ikaba zifite umutungo ugera kuri miliyali 301 Frw byerekana ko ibijyanye n'ubwizigame abaturage batangiye ku byumva neza.

Aya kandi yiyongeraho ayandi arenga miliyali 95 Frw, amaze kuzigamwa n'abari murii 'Ejo Heza'.

Umuyobozi w'Intara y'Iburasirazuba, Pudence Rubingisa, avuga ko kuba izuba ryaravuye rigatinda ari ibintu bamaze kumenyera kandi bakwiye no kugira ingamba zihoraho zo guhangana nabyo.

Ati "Ni ibintu bibaho buri mwaka biba bisaba ko twiteganyiriza, mu gushaka imyaka ihangana n'iryo hindagurika ry'ikirere, ntidutere bya bihingwa tumenyereye kandi bisaba imvura nyinshi tudafite muri ibyo bice."

Aha kandi ubuyobozi buvuga ko harimo no gushakwa indi mirimo ibafasha kuzamura imibereho y'abaturage idashingiye cyane ku buhinzi butegereza ibisubizo ku kirere.

Abaturage bashishikarizwa kumva no kumenya ko na duke umuntu afite ashobora kuzigamamo, kuko bidasaba ko umuntu aba afite ibya mirenge kugira ngo abone ayo azigama.

President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne are considering extending trade and investment between Africa and the Caribbean.

Kagame while attending the four-day 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting at Jumby Bay Island on November 3 held discussions with the Premeir of the Caribbean Nation.

The two leaders pledged to strengthen relations between their countries and encourage closer cooperation between the two regions.

Meanwhile, Browne encouraged greater engagement between African and Caribbean businesses, including efforts to identify products and services that could create mutually beneficial commercial opportunities.

He added that current global challenges present opportunities for countries of the Global South to deepen cooperation and establish stronger economic partnerships.

Browne reaffirmed Antigua and Barbuda’s willingness to support Rwanda on matters of mutual interest, including international candidatures, and assured Kagame that the country would remain a reliable partner.

The Rwandan leader, in turn, congratulated Browne on Antigua and Barbuda’s hosting of CHOGM 2026 and expressed his government’s interest in building closer relations with the country and the wider Commonwealth.

Browne, is also serving as Commonwealth Chair-in-Office.

MN202611_1e0h0qh8y53.t:
Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.

The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case.

The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros.

It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home.

His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games.

A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste.

Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well.

So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years.

Such a pattern appears with almost every man who sat on the Portuguese bench - there were clashes, but also communion with managers and team-mates that help explain this ending.

Six tournaments, 11 goals - Ronaldo's World Cup legacy

Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football

What legacy does Cristiano Ronaldo leave on the international stage?

When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance.

He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal.

The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way.

A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere.

It was a painful way to learn what a final costs, and it left him with a hunger that never really went away.

Figo owned the number 7 at the time, so Ronaldo had to have 17. Figo helped him settle but had no intention of making it easy. When he left the national team in 2006, the shirt and the team became Ronaldo's.

In September 2005, before a qualifier in Russia, Scolari and Figo went to his room to tell him his father had died. Scolari offered to send him home. Ronaldo chose to play, asked his team-mates to behave as normal, and spent time in the dressing room doing ball tricks.

That was his way to cope with the expected but still hugely hurtful passing of his alcoholic dad. He later called Scolari "father". That way the national team had become the place that held him together.

Things went sour with Carlos Queiroz. After the 2010 World Cup exit against Spain, asked to explain a poor performance, Ronaldo told journalists to ask the coach. His influence in the camp had grown so large it changed routines and habits, which explains why the coach felt undermined.

The sociologist Joao Nuno Coelho offers the best lens on how Portugal sees him. In his analysis, the national team became a representation of Portuguese identity and of the country's need to be seen internationally.

In years of economic hardship and a crisis of confidence, a team that won admiration abroad was important beyond football.

Ronaldo stood at the centre of that need and created contradictory feelings. Some Portuguese questioned his individualism and his ego, and not everyone saw themselves in his personality.

Coelho explains criticising him became more difficult as time went by. The country wanted to be proud of him and sometimes felt uneasy at the same time.

The former international Jorge Andrade told me some supporters preferred figures like Figo, Eusebio, Paulo Futre or Rui Costa. Even so, Portugal was proud to have him. And with the titles, the doubts eased.

'Ronaldo's records will never be broken'

Under Fernando Santos in 2016, he changed. He accepted playing as a centre forward next to Nani - he had never taken a coach's instructions so naturally.

After the opening draw with Iceland, he told Nani in private that he trusted Santos, and the dressing room began to see a real captain. After missing a penalty against Austria, he barely slept. Santos woke up and found him already awake.

At the training camp in Marcoussis, he took a fan's megaphone and told supporters Portugal had won nothing yet. He was enjoying the leadership role.

In the final in Paris, he left the pitch in tears, injured. He had not had the best tournament, with a muscle complaint that did not let him perform at his best.

Nani took the armband. At half-time Ronaldo pulled himself together to encourage his team-mates, and before extra time, still limping, he told Eder he would score.

But the old instinct never fully disappeared. During extra-time, Ronaldo stood in the technical area giving orders until the fourth official sent him back. Other coaches I consulted found it excessive.

His greatest strength, the need to influence every result, also made limits hard to accept.

When he debuted in 2003, Portugal was still searching for its first major title. Some players mark an era, and others change a national team for good. He belongs to the second group.

That night in July 2016 gave Portugal its first European Championship.

Three years later he scored a hat-trick against Switzerland to put them into the first Nations League final, which Portugal won. In 2025 he lifted a second Nations League at an age when most players have retired.

No one has scored more goals for a national side, and no one has pulled on the Portugal shirt more times.

Under his influence, Portugal stopped being a gifted team and became one that arrives at every tournament expecting to contend, while a whole generation of players came through a dressing room where he decided what the standard was.

Coelho's point holds here as well: a small country found a way to be noticed, and for two decades he was its face.

After 2016 the question around him changed. Fewer asked whether he was selfish, and more asked whether Portugal depended on him too much.

Ronaldo scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for Portugal

In the World Cup in 2018, he scored three against Spain, including a free-kick after 45 attempts in major tournaments, and the team still went out to Uruguay.

After a difficult 2026 World Cup, much was made of him still starting up front when in fact statistically that was his best period.

Under Roberto Martinez, with 28 goals in 37 games, 0.756 per match, improves the 0.624 with Santos.

The federation has announced a special tribute to honour his contribution, and that is necessary as the exit has not left fans room for a celebration they want to be part of.

Not only they grew up with him, he took them to places they had not yet been.

Ahavuye isanamu, Ministère de l'Intérieur de la R.D Congo/X

Minisitiri w'ubutegetsi bw'igihugu muri Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo, Jacquemain Shabani, yihanangirije abanyamuryango b'ihuriro ry'abatavuga rumwe n'ubutegetsi rya C64, ababurira ko bashobora guhanishwa igifungo kiri hagati y'umwaka umwe n'imyaka itanu baramutse bagiye mu mujyi wa Goma, mu burasirazuba bw'igihugu, guhura na Joseph Kabila wahoze ari Perezida w'icyo gihugu.

Ibi byatangajwe n'ikinyamakuru Mediacongo.net cyigenga, ku wa 4 Ugushyingo (11).

Iri burira rije rikurikira inama yahuje abayobozi batanu ba C64 yabereye i Roma mu Butaliyani. Muri iyo nama, batangaje ko bateganya kugirana ibiganiro bitandukanye na Perezida Félix Tshisekedi ndetse na Joseph Kabila, mu rwego rwo gushaka ibisubizo by'ibibazo bya politiki n'umutekano byugarije igihugu.

Mu magambo yavugiye mu bitangazamakuru byo muri icyo gihugu tariki 4 ukwa 11, Shabani yasubiyemo ingingo ya 122 y'Itegeko Mpana byaha rya Congo, iteganya igifungo cy'umwaka umwe kugeza ku myaka itanu ku muntu ukomeza kugirana umubano n'abahagarariye igihugu gifatwa nk'umwanzi mu gihe cy'intambara, atabiherewe uburenganzira na Leta.

Minisitiri yavuze ko abanyapolitiki bagirana imikoranire n'abantu bari mu duce tugenzurwa n'ihuriro rya gisirikare na politiki ryitwa Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), riyobowe na Kabila, bashobora kuba bakurikiranwa hashingiwe kuri iryo tegeko.

Shabani yanavuze ku kuba Kabila ari mu mujyi wa Goma, umurwa mukuru w'Intara ya Kivu ya Ruguru. Yasobanuye ko mu ntangiriro inzego z'ubuyobozi zari zarabwiwe ko uwahoze ari Perezida yari yagiye muri uwo mujyi mu rwego rwo kwitabira ibiganiro bigamije amahoro, ariko nyuma zikaza kugera ku mwanzuro w'uko yari yifatanyije n'imitwe irwanya ubutegetsi.

Joseph Kabila yakomeje guhakana inshuro nyinshi ibirego bimushinja ibikorwa bigamije kurwanya ubutegetsi cyangwa gukorana n'inyeshyamba zo mu mutwe wa M23, ushyigikiwe n'u Rwanda.

Ku rundi ruhande, ku wa 4 Ugushyingo, umuyobozi w'abatavuga rumwe n'ubutegetsi muri Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo, Moïse Katumbi, yatangaje ko we, Martin Fayulu na Augustin Matata Ponyo wahoze ari Minisitiri w'Intebe, bateganya kujyana i Goma guhura na Joseph Kabila.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Mu kiganiro cyasohotse kuri uwo munsi, Katumbi yavuze ko urwo rugendo ruzakorwa mu izina ry'ihuriro C64 n'abafatanyabikorwa baryo, aho kuba gahunda ye bwite.

Yavuze ko yaba we cyangwa Augustin Matata Ponyo nta gahunda bafite yo kujya i Kinshasa, asobanura ko bari mu buhungiro. Yongeyeho ko bazerekeza i Goma barangije uruzinduko barimo muri iki gihe.

Katumbi yavuze ko itariki y'urwo ruzinduko itaramenyekana, ariko ashimangira ko izatangazwa ku mugaragaro kandi ko inama bazagirana na Kabila itazaba iy'ibanga.

Yanenze kandi ibyo yise amahame abiri atandukanye akoreshwa na leta, yibaza impamvu ubutegetsi bwiteguye kugirana ibiganiro n'umutwe wa M23 i Doha, ariko bukarwanya ko abatavuga rumwe na bwo bagirana ibiganiro na Kabila, uwo ashimangira ko ari umuturage wa Congo.

Urwo rugendo ruteganyijwe mu gihe hakomeje ibikorwa by'abanyapolitiki n'abayobozi bo mu karere bigamije gushaka igisubizo cy'amahoro binyuze mu biganiro ku ntambara ikomeje mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, aho umutwe wa M23 ugenzura ibice byinshi by'ubutaka

MN202611_10shgqwad7q.t:
Sir Tom Jones has had to postpone recent shows due to ill health

Sir Tom Jones has told fans he feared his life was "over" after being admitted to hospital in the US with flu.

The 86-year-old from Pontypridd spent a week at the Ronald Regan UCLA Medical Center in Los Angeles and was forced to cancel or reschedule a number of concerts.

But on Wednesday night, he was back on stage at the Greek Theatre and told the audience just how serious his "bad case of the flu" was.

"[I thought] Oh well, this is it, you've had a wonderful life, Tommy, but it's over right now," he said.

"I must say this, in the UCLA, they really did a wonderful job. So I'm here."

"[The medical staff said] What do you want to do now? I was in there for a week. And I said, 'I've got to get back on the stage'. This is where I belong. I can't live without this, believe me."

Sir Tom recently made headlines after revealing ITV had "made the decision" to "fire" him from The Voice UK coaching panel , having served as an coach on the singing competition since its debut in 2012.

In the latest series, and his last as a coach, he mentored Welsh singer Cate McHugh to victory .

McHugh previously told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast that being chosen to be on Team Tom at the blind audition was "absolutely undescribable".

Sir Tom Jones has appeared as an on-off coach on the singing competition since it premiered in 2012

The Delilah and It's Not Unusual singer has achieved three UK number one singles and four chart-topping albums during a music career spanning more than six decades.

His awards include one Grammy and two Brits, and in 2006 he received a knighthood from the late Queen Elizabeth II for services to music.

He is next due to perform at the Yaamava' Theater in San Bernadino, California on Friday.

Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru mu Rwanda, FERWAFA, ryatangaje ibisabwa ku waba yifuza gusaba akazi ko kuba Umuyobozi Ushinzwe Tekiniki ku rwego rw’Igihugu [DTN], usimbura Umufaransa wagiye, Gérard Buscher.

Mu kwezi gushize ni bwo ubuyobozi bwa FERWAFA, bwasezeye ku mugaragaro uwari DTN mu myaka ine ishize, Gérard Buscher nyuma y’uko yari asoje amasezerano ye, ntiyongerwe andi.

FERWAFA ibicishije ku rubuga rwayo [Website], yatangaje ko yatangiye gushaka umusimbura wa Gérard. Iri Shyirahamwe ryavuze ko ubyifuza agomba kuba yamaze kubisaba bitarenze ku wa 20 Ugushyingo 2026.

Iri Shyirahamwe ryashyizeho ibisabwa kugira ngo usaba aka kazi abe yagahabwa. Harimo kuba afite uburambe mu bijyanye n’imiyoborere ya Tekiniki y’umupira w’amaguru.

Harimo kugira ubumenyi ku mitoreze no ku Iterambere ry’abafite impano mu gukina ruhago.

Kugaragaza gahunda y’igihe kirekire mu kuza impano zitandukanye mu byiciro by’imyaka bitandukanye ndetse no gukurikirana amakipe n’ingengo z’imari.

Kugira ubushake n’ubumenyi kuri ruhago y’abagore no kurengera abakinnyi no kugira Indangagaciro z’Imiyoborere.

Kuba avuga kandi yandika neza ururimo rw’Icyongereza n’Igifaransa. Kuba yiteguye gukorera mu Rwanda.

Kugira Impamyabumenyi ya Kaminuza cyangwa Impamyabumenyi ya ruhago mu bijyanye na Tekiniki.

Kuba yarize ibijyanye n’imiyoborere muri FIFA cyangwa muri CAF. Kugira Impamyabumenyi za CAF, UEFA cyangwa izizisimbura zo kuyindi Migabane.

Kugira ubunararibonye mu bijyanye n’amashyirahamwe ya ruhago. Kugira ubumenyi kuri ruhago ya Afurika. Ibi biri mu nyongera nziza ku by’usaba aka kazi.

Agomba kandi kuba afite uburaribonye mu gufasha ruhago y’abato mu bakobwa n’abahungu [Grassroots].

Usaba akazi, agomba gutanga ibaruwa igasaba ndetse n’umwirondoro ugaragaza usaba akazi n’uburambe afite [CV].

Mu gusaba akazi kandi, usaba agomba kugaragaza Impamyabumenyi z’ibyasabwe byose.

Agomba kugaragaza mu buryo bw’inyandiko, umushinga wo guteza imbere ruhago mu myaka itatu iri imbere. Agomba kugaragaza abantu byibura babiri bahamya ko bamuzi muri uwo mwuga.

Abujuje ibisabwa, bagomba kubyohereza kuri careers@ferwafa.com.

MN202611_1qlrw3a46vo.t:
Mu kiganiro yagiranye n’Abanyekongo baba mu Burusiya ku wa 30 Ukwakira, Tshisekedi yavuze ko ubutegetsi bwe burimo gukorakoranya abarwanyi ba FDLR i Kitona, bikaba bigaragara ko bushobora kuba burimo gutegura kubohereza mu kindi gihugu.

Ibi bituma hibazwa ikibazo cy’ingenzi: Kuki Kinshasa irimo kuganira ku kwimura abarwanyi ba FDLR aho kubahiriza ibyo yiyemeje byo guca intege no gusenya ubushobozi bw’uwo mutwe?

Amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington si gahunda yo kwimura abarwanyi. Asaba ko hafatwa ingamba zifatika z’umutekano zigamije gukemura ikibazo cy’iterabwoba ritewe na FDLR.

Kwimura bamwe mu barwanyi bayo bakava ahantu hamwe bajyanwa ahandi, cyangwa bakoherezwa ku butaka bw’ikindi gihugu, ntibisobanura gusenya uwo mutwe, gukuraho ubushobozi bwawo bwa gisirikare cyangwa guhangana n’ingengabitekerezo ya jenoside ushingiyeho. Ahubwo ni ukwimurira ahandi ikibazo cyari gihari.

Ibivuguruzanya mu bayobozi ba Congo bituma iki kibazo kirushaho gutera impungenge

Hasigaye iminsi ibiri gusa ngo Tshisekedi atangaze ibyo, Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga wa RDC, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, yabwiye televiziyo ya RT ko igihugu cye kidashobora kwambura imbunda FDLR kuko abarwanyi bayo bakorera mu bice bigenzurwa na M23.

Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma, Patrick Muyaya, na we yagiye atanga ibisobanuro bisa n’ibyo inshuro nyinshi, igihe Kinshasa ibazwa impamvu itarashyira mu bikorwa inshingano zayo zo guhangana na FDLR.

Nyamara ubu Perezida w’icyo gihugu arimo kubwira amahanga ko ubutegetsi bwe bwakorakoranyirije abarwanyi ba FDLR i Kitona.

None se amahanga akwiye kwemera iyihe mvugo? Niba abarwanyi ba FDLR badashobora kugerwaho kuko bakorera mu bice bigenzurwa na M23, Kinshasa yabashije ite kubakorakoranyiriza i Kitona? Niba Guverinoma ishoboye kubashyira hamwe ahantu runaka hagenewe gukusanyirizwamo, ni iki kiyibuza gukomeza ikabambura intwaro, ikanaca intege ubushobozi bw’uwo mutwe?

FDLR ntishobora kubura mu magambo ya Guverinoma ku wa Mbere, ku wa Kabiri ikavugwa ko iri mu bice bigenzurwa na M23, ku wa Gatatu ikongera kugaragara i Kitona, hanyuma ku wa Kane ikibazo cyayo kikitirirwa ikindi gihugu. Kinshasa ifitiye amahanga umwenda wo gutanga ibisobanuro bihamye kandi bitavuguruzanya.

Ahari ikivuguruzanya kurushaho ni uburyo Tshisekedi ubwe asobanura iki kibazo mu bya politiki. Yakunze gushinja u Rwanda gukoresha FDLR nk’urwitwazo rw’impungenge zarwo z’umutekano ndetse n’uruhare ruvugwa ko rufite mu burasirazuba bwa RDC. Yigeze no kugaragaza ko atishimiye igitutu Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika ishyira kuri Guverinoma ye kugira ngo ice intege uwo mutwe.

Ariko niba FDLR ari urwitwazo gusa, nk’uko Tshisekedi abivuga, kuki arwanya igikorwa ubwacyo cyakuraho urwo rwitwazo? Ni gute umuntu yimura urwitwazo akaruha ikindi gihugu? Kandi kuki yitotomba ku gitutu mpuzamahanga gisaba gusenya umutwe witwaje intwaro, kandi igihugu cye cyamaze kwiyemeza mu nyandiko kuwuca intege no kuwusenyera ubushobozi?

FDLR si umutwe ubaho mu bitekerezo gusa. Amateka yawo, ingengabitekerezo ya jenoside ndetse n’ibikorwa byawo bikomeje kugaragara mu burasirazuba bwa RDC ni ibintu byanditsweho kandi bizwi. Guca intege uwo mutwe si igikorwa cyo kugirira neza u Rwanda, ahubwo ni inshingano mu rwego rw’umutekano ndetse n’intambwe y’ingenzi iganisha ku mahoro arambye mu karere.

Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zagize uruhare rukomeye mu korohereza isinywa ry’amasezerano ya Washington. Ubu icyizere ayo masezerano ashingiyeho kizaterwa n’uko hazagenzurwa ko ibyo abayashyizeho umukono biyemeje bihinduka ibikorwa bifatika kandi bishobora kugenzurwa.

Tshisekedi ntashobora gushyira umukono ku masezerano asaba ko FDLR icibwa intege, nyuma akinubira igitutu cyo kuyashyira mu bikorwa, hanyuma akerekana ko kuyimura ari bwo buryo bwo gukemura ikibazo.

Washington ikwiye gusaba ibisobanuro bisobanutse: Ni abarwanyi bangahe ba FDLR, niba bahari, bari i Kitona? Ese bambuwe intwaro? Biteganyijwe ko imiyoborere y’uwo mutwe n’imiyoboro yawo ya gisirikare bizagenda bite? Ni ayahe masezerano cyangwa uburyo bw’amategeko Kinshasa ishingiraho umugambi wo kubohereza mu kindi gihugu?

Ikibazo nyamukuru ntikikiri ukumenya icyo Kinshasa isabwa gukora, ahubwo ni ukumenya niba ifite ubushake bwa politiki bwo kugikora. Kandi Washington izakomeza kugeza ryari kurebera ntigire icyo ikora kuri uku kudashyira mu bikorwa ibyo RDC yiyemeje?

SHANGHAI – Rwanda is showcasing coffee, tea, honey, chili and other locally produced goods at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which opened in Shanghai on November 5, as the country seeks to expand its exports to the Chinese market.

The six-day exhibition, running until November 10 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center, brings together businesses and potential buyers from around the world.

Rwanda is presenting a range of products, including specialty coffee, tea, chili, dried fruits, natural honey, macadamia nuts and handicrafts. The country is also using the exhibition to promote investment, tourism and cultural exchange.

Rwanda’s participation comes as the two countries mark 55 years of diplomatic relations, with economic cooperation expanding in recent years.

Bilateral trade between Rwanda and China reached approximately $849 million in 2025, up from $300 million in 2019, according to figures released alongside Rwanda’s participation at the expo.

Rwanda’s exports to China increased from $35 million in 2019 to $227 million in 2025, representing growth of approximately 549%.

Chinese investment registered in Rwanda also increased from $460 million in 2024 to $548.5 million in 2025, a rise of 19%. Chinese companies have investments in manufacturing, infrastructure, construction, energy and real estate.

Rwanda’s Ambassador to China, Lt Gen (Rtd) Emmanuel Karenzi Karake, said the expo provides an important opportunity for local businesses, particularly smallholder farmers and women-led cooperatives, to reach Chinese consumers and establish lasting commercial partnerships.

“CIIE has proven to be an invaluable platform for Rwandan enterprises, particularly smallholder farmers and women-led cooperatives, to access the Chinese market and build lasting business partnerships,” he said.

He encouraged Rwandan businesses to take advantage of the exhibition to connect with buyers and investors and explore new opportunities.

The country’s participation includes coffee cupping, tea tasting, cultural performances and business matchmaking sessions intended to connect Rwandan exhibitors with Chinese buyers, distributors and e-commerce platforms.

An additional opportunity comes from China’s zero-tariff treatment for all Rwandan goods, which took effect on December 1, 2024.

The arrangement allows eligible Rwandan products to enter the Chinese market without import tariffs, subject to rules of origin, customs procedures and product-specific requirements.

Rwanda and China announced a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in September 2024, building on cooperation in trade, investment and industrial development under the Belt and Road Initiative and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

Beyond promoting agricultural exports, Rwanda is using the expo to attract investors to sectors including manufacturing, agro-processing and energy, with an emphasis on increasing local value addition.

The CIIE, launched in 2018, has become a platform for international businesses seeking access to the Chinese consumer market.

MN202611_jdtpapmlrj.t:
Interest rates have risen to 4% and the Bank of England has indicated there are more rises to come. The question is how many? There is a split on the rate-setting committee here.

Three of the nine voting members referred to "rises" plural. One member voted for a bigger increase, to 4.25%. Three referred to just one more including governor Andrew Bailey.

My read on this is that the expectation is for one more rise in February. Two and done, but it depends.

It is painful for those on variable mortgages, but should not be seen as the start of a cycle of hikes.

Predicting where interest rates will go is like throwing darts at a board that constantly moves around the wall, with expectations of how long the Iran War will last and its impact on the economy and prices lurching from day to day.

The Bank's forecasts indicate inflation is heading to just under 5% next spring as a typical household energy bill surges by 27% in January to £2,150 a year.

Why have they raised now? High and rising inflation risks a further cycle of self fulfilling expectations of rising prices. It hasn't been seen so far, however. The war has lasted for 9 months, and led to oil prices used in the forecast averaging $108 a barrel.

And yet on the day they have announced the rate rise, the oil price is actually 13% lower than that having fallen in the run up and after the US mid term elections, reflecting expectations or guesses that President Trump will now retreat or deescalate from the Iran war.

The other notable factor is that the UK economy is performing much better than forecasts and expectations. This is underlined by the Bank of England's latest forecasts.

Growth has been 0.6%, and 0.5% in the first two quarters of the year. It is heading for 0.7%, the Bank said, between July and September, before slowing in the three months to the end of the year. Unemployment has stabilised, actually falling a little.

Some of this has fed through into a better performing currency , with sterling at its highest level since the Brexit referendum, when measured against a basket of currencies. This can help rein in inflation by making imports cheaper.

So, this is an unusual type of uncertainty. Even the expected further rise, probably in February next year is conditional on the war continuing.

The Bank of England stopped waiting for President Trump's war to end today, but perhaps the Democrats' resounding victory in the US midterm elections will stop the inflationary wave? The Bank has thrown a tentative first dart, and there is probably another to come.

Interest rates have been raised for the first time in more than three years - and it could be good and bad news for you.

Here are three ways the increase to 4% from 3.75% could affect you.

Rate-setters at the Bank make changes to interest rates to fulfil their role of keeping price rises at a steady level.

Higher rates are meant to encourage people to spend less, reducing demand for goods and services and limiting price rises.

This impacts businesses in two ways - less money to spend among their customers may mean they sell less, but also the cost of borrowing to invest as a company goes up.

Many businesses, particularly small ones, have variable rate loans which are influenced by the Bank rate.

Firms say higher rates limit their ability to offer new jobs and wage rises.

Mitchell Barnes, founder and chief executive of Ryse 3D, which manufactures 3D parts for the defence and automotive sectors, said the "reality" of rising interest rates was to look at the cost of employees and people.

That could include greater use of robots rather than workers.

"It's going to cause issues with, I suppose, employment across all sectors for people," he said.

"You're going to see reduced employment, more automation, more robotics being put into facilities, just in order to increase efficiency and make that money go further."

The Bank rate - and where it is expected to go in future - has a significant impact on the interest rates customers are offered on savings products.

So, if you're saving up for something quite expensive, like a holiday, or very expensive, like a home, then a rate rise could be good news.

When interest rates were low throughout the 2010s, the returns for savers were poor, but borrowing costs were low too.

The answer then and now, according to experts, is to make sure you move your savings to benefit from the best possible rates.

What's happening to UK interest rates and what does it mean for mortgages?

You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go?

Leaving your savings in an old account (a product not offered to new customers), rather than shopping around, can mean you are penalised for your loyalty.

"Savers have endured years of unrewarded loyalty, with those leaving [a £20,000 cash pot] in closed accounts losing out on an extra £139 over the past three years compared to on-sale easy access accounts," said Rachel Springall, from financial information service Moneyfacts.

She also said locking away your money for longer, with a fixed-term deal, is usually more lucrative.

The other flipside is that renting while you save could get more expensive, because a rising Bank rate may well increase costs for landlords.

The big losers from a rate rise are those who borrow money, and specifically those on variable rate mortgages.

About 500,000 homeowners have a mortgage that "tracks" the Bank of England's rate.

Any rise in the Bank rate means an increase in the monthly repayments on their outstanding loan. For a typical loan, the cost is going up by about £31 a month now the Bank has raised the base rate, but it depends on the size of people's loans.

An additional 500,000 homeowners on standard variable rates (SVRs) must wait to see if their lender chooses to pass on any Bank rate rise. Typically, this would mean a £14 increase per month in repayments for a 0.25 percentage points rates rise.

If you, like 87% of mortgage-holders, have a fixed-rate deal, then the payments will stay the same until the end of your current deal, which is usually two or five years.

While monthly payments are not immediately affected by a rate change, future deals are. Lenders had already "priced in" the latest rate rise when quoting new deals. Expectations for the Bank rate into next year are crucial on what they offer next.

The average rate on fixed deals are much higher now than was predicted at the start of the year. It means those remortgaging, possibly after the post-Covid boom in the housing market, are facing the prospect of higher mortgage payments.

Some people have been choosing to move onto tracker deals instead, taking a view - including some risk - of the Bank rate not moving towards a series of further hikes.

Do you have a mortgage, a credit card, a car finance agreement? How are interest rates affecting you?

Kozo Tashima became president of the Japan Football Association in 2016

The Japan Football Association honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has announced his intention to stand against Gianni Infantino to be the next Fifa president.

Tashima, 68, is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach.

He said he wants to convey "integrity, soundness, and high moral standards" and "contribute to a better future for football".

Infantino has been under intense scrutiny since it emerged he had been planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was abandoned at the end of July, after significant backlash from across world football.

The deadline for candidates to stand in the election is 18 November.

Whilst support for Infantino was severely impacted by the FFE scandal, he has shored up support in recent months.

Infantino told BBC Sport last month that he felt he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football as he bids for a fourth term in charge of Fifa.

His comments came after he was "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put their name forward in October for next year's Fifa presidential election.

However, Tashima's emergence as a challenger - with the backing of the Japan Football Association (JFA) - will now test the strength of Infantino's supporter base.

As with all candidates, Tashima will require the backing of five Fifa member associations.

Infantino laughs off resignation questions

Announcing his intentions, Tashima said: "I believe it is important to clearly communicate to the world of football the integrity, soundness, and high moral standards that Japanese football has cherished and built up over the years.

"I have decided to run for Fifa presidential election in order to convey this philosophy to the world and contribute to a better future for football.

"I will take on this challenge with strong determination, making use of the experience I have cultivated so far, and contributing to the further development of world football."

Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, president of the JFA, said: "This decision is a major challenge to contribute to the further development of world football by utilising that experience and knowledge, and at the same time, we believe it will be an opportunity to show the world the ideals and attitudes that Japanese football has cherished."

MN202611_15nqzn4ix1q.t:
Laura Kaminski guided Crystal Palace to the WSL 2 title in 2024

When English manager Laura Kaminski was approached to become the head coach of Norwegian club SK Brann in January, she could not turn it down.

She jumped at the opportunity to move abroad and develop her coaching skills and is even competing for a place in the Europa Cup quarter-finals next Wednesday.

It was a decision that paid off as 10 months later, she is celebrating a Norwegian league and cup double after a dream debut season.

"My time in the city [of Bergen] has been brilliant," the 38-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I can't go to the supermarket at the minute because so many people are stopping me to wish me congratulations, which is so nice.

"I'm over the moon and it was nice to get the title done before the last game so we can relax. I thought it was going to go right to the wire.

"It's been a competitive year. I've enjoyed every minute. We had a great night with all our fans, who were waiting for us to return from Oslo."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Kaminski on the challenges for English coaches in WSL

Kaminski described it as a "hectic" year as she moved from London to Norway and away from her family to take on the Brann job.

The Englishwoman had spent over a year at Crystal Palace, where she led them to promotion to the Women's Super League in 2024.

She was sacked in February 2025 after a tough WSL season as Palace struggled to compete with better financially-backed clubs.

However, she is regarded as one of the country's brightest female managers and has added to her CV with her experiences in Norway.

"I've learned a lot. It's been chaotic - I counted that I have taken 65 flights in 11 months - so it's been exhausting, but what an experience!" added Kaminski.

"To go all the way up to the Arctic Circle and play away [games] in freezing cold conditions with horizontal snow, to beautiful days in Bergen.

"Palace was totally different to Brann. I'm at a club that expects to win the Toppserien [the Norwegian top-flight] as they believe they have invested the most.

"That's been a real challenge. The WSL is dominated by the favourites in the pack so it wasn't always the expectation to get three points against big teams [at Palace]."

Kaminski admits being away from loved ones is "hard" and she has had to be prepared to "make sacrifices" but Brann's trophy success makes it worth it.

She has also picked up new ideas for her coaching philosophy having experienced the high-risk, attack-minded football in Norway.

"Norwegian teams are almost guaranteed to concede every game because they play such attacking football with no fear, and a relentlessness to press," she added.

"That is a bit different to what I was used to. When I watched the tactical displays when I first came in, I was a little bit alarmed at what people were doing.

"But when you play against their sides, and against that [pressing], it is really difficult. It's given me a lot of fuel for the future.

"There are some really fit, fast and athletic players here. It's not a surprise that big, big clubs are coming in for them."

Laura Kaminski spent a year and a half at Crystal Palace

After a season in Norway, Kaminski believes she is a better coach.

She had spent over 15 years as an assistant manager at various clubs in the WSL 2 and WSL and a coaching role with England's under-19s before joining Palace.

But having added European experience to her CV, Kaminski hopes it will open the door to more opportunities in the future.

"I'd like to think I've got a well-rounded skillset to be able to manage at the top level. Right now, my focus is on Brann and a new chapter," said Kaminski.

"There's only two levels in England that are professional. I definitely wanted to get European exposure, which I was never going to get in England.

"At the time, I was in discussions with a few clubs but it was things that I'd done before, or the project wasn't matching.

"I knew that when I came to Brann, I was going to coach top-level players. I wanted to be at the top of the competition and I was desperate to win a trophy."

Kaminski has urged other female coaches in England to go abroad and gain experience as she believes opportunities are too few in the WSL.

A study from UK Coaching in October showed there has been a 6% decline in the overall number of female coaches in recent years.

There are currently three English female coaches in the WSL - Jo Potter at Crystal Palace, Amy Merricks at Birmingham City and Karen Hills at Charlton Athletic - and they all came up with promoted clubs this summer.

But Kaminski says she is "concerned" about where they might go next and hopes more opportunities in English men's football will open up soon.

"I ended up leaving the country to go and get what I thought I deserved and had earned the right to work in, in terms of the level," said Kaminski.

"There's more than one female out there that's capable [of working in men's football]. I don't think it's out of reach. I would always, certainly, be open to it.

"At the moment, for me, there's not enough consideration even for that opportunity to be given to female managers who are more than capable.

"I think the foundations are there for females to take the plunge but is the world of football ready? I'm unsure."

Money, family and sexism - why the number of women coaches is dropping

MN202611_1h46zs1vrsv.t:
Bill Gates and Health Minister Dr Sabin Nsanzimana visited Rwanda’s National Health Intelligence Centre, which uses real-time healthcare data and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve service delivery.

KIGALI – Rwanda could add about US$237 million to its economy over the next decade by capitalising on artificial intelligence, but the country faces significant gaps in preparing young people to benefit from the technology, a new study has found.

The Ayre Index, unveiled at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2026) in Antigua and Barbuda, ranks Rwanda 47th among 56 Commonwealth countries for youth artificial intelligence readiness.

Rwanda scored 38.1 out of 100, below the study’s readiness benchmark of 53 – but scores high when compared to African peers. Only 15 Commonwealth countries reached or exceeded the benchmark.

The study estimates that artificial intelligence could increase Rwanda’s gross domestic product by US$237 million after 10 years under its moderate scenario. The estimated increase ranges from US$115 million under a conservative scenario to US$360 million under an optimistic one.

The figures are not annual gains or forecasts of accumulated economic growth. They represent possible effects on the level of gross domestic product after 10 years, based on economic scenarios developed by the International Monetary Fund and applied by researchers to Rwanda’s 2025 gross domestic product.

Rwanda has relatively strong digital infrastructure by regional standards. The study says 4G mobile coverage reaches 98.8% of the population, while electricity reaches 72%. It also describes data prices as comparatively affordable among Commonwealth countries.

But researchers say a lack of public data makes it difficult to establish how young Rwandans are actually using artificial intelligence, particularly for education, employment and business.

The gap could make it harder for policymakers and development partners to identify where investment and training are most needed.

Rwanda has about four million people aged between 15 and 29, according to the study. Researchers say the country could build on its existing digital infrastructure by expanding practical learning and improving access to opportunities that allow young people to use artificial intelligence productively.

The study identifies five priorities: affordable and reliable access to technology; practical skills in education; stronger links between training, employment and enterprise; artificial intelligence tools adapted to local languages and needs; and safeguards that allow young people to question automated decisions.

Calvin Ayre, founder of the Ayre Think Tank, said the ability of young people to gain skills and use new technology would determine whether countries benefit from the artificial intelligence transition.

“AI is going to change how we work, how we do business and how wealth is created,” Ayre said.

The index covers all 56 Commonwealth countries and draws on 1,128 sources, including official statistics, international databases, surveys and published studies. It assesses conditions that could help people aged 15 to 29 benefit from artificial intelligence.

Singapore topped the ranking with 77.6 points, followed by Malta with 75 and Australia with 71.

The researchers caution that the index measures conditions associated with readiness rather than the artificial intelligence competence of individual young people. They also note that data comes from different years and age groups, while some indicators rely on estimates or other published substitutes.

For Rwanda, the findings point to a gap between having the infrastructure to access artificial intelligence and having the skills, evidence and opportunities needed to turn that access into economic gains.

MN202611_1ohrtfeq9d.t:
Married at First Sight UK cancelled after rape allegations

Married at First Sight UK will not return, Channel 4 has said, following a BBC investigation into the hit reality TV show.

The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis earlier this year, after Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show , while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.

A review was commissioned by Channel 4 shortly after the BBC first contacted the broadcaster, with details of the allegations we had heard.

On Thursday, the completed review recommended extra safeguards on the show. But Channel 4 said the programme had "run its course" and apologised to the women involved in the investigation.

The broadcaster's chief executive Priya Dogra said she was "very sorry for the distress those women have clearly felt", adding that the show's budget would be reinvested in "distinctive new programming".

The Panorama investigation in May, in which three women made allegations about the men they were partnered with - claims the men deny, made the following allegations:

One woman said her onscreen husband raped her and threatened her with an acid attack.

A second woman told both Channel 4 and CPL, before broadcast, about being allegedly raped by her onscreen husband. Her episodes were still aired.

A third woman - Shona Manderson, the only woman who was identified - accused her onscreen husband of sexual misconduct.

All three women accused the show of not doing enough to protect them.

Lawyers for CPL, the independent production company that makes the UK version of the show, previously said its welfare system is "gold standard" and industry-leading, and that it acted appropriately in all these cases.

Channel 4 had initially told Panorama that all the allegations were "wholly uncorroborated".

Dame Caroline Dinenage MP, chair of the House of Commons culture and media committee, said the decision to axe the show "makes sense" given the review's findings and the "seriousness of the allegations".

"Reality TV contestants have often been treated as a commodity, with duty of care a slogan rather than a genuine principle. Everyone involved in producing and regulating reality TV must now learn and act," she added.

A spokesman for Ofcom said the broadcast regulator would "carefully consider the reports published today as we move to strengthen our guidance for broadcasters".

"We are clear that broadcasters have a duty of care towards members of the public who participate in their programmes."

What is your reaction to the cancellation of MAFS UK?

The review into the show was split into two - one part examined welfare protocols on MAFS UK, and the other reported on how Channel 4 handled the allegations.

The review into welfare protocols, led by former BBC One Controller Lorraine Heggessey, concluded that some parts of the programme's format increased "the risk profile of the show".

Although she found the protocols for MAFS UK were extremely thorough and of a high standard, she said "intimacy is a key focus", and that "some elements of the show could implicitly put pressure on contributors to be intimate".

Heggessey made suggestions including installing CCTV in all areas of the apartments, constantly monitored by a welfare team, with panic buttons and "safe words" in place.

She concluded that, with enhancements to the existing welfare framework and adjustments to the format, it would have been reasonable to continue to produce future series of MAFS UK.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's PM programme on Thursday, she added that the suggested changes "would have, in lots of ways, changed both the format and the nature of the show, but would have given the kind of protection that both Channel Four and CPL would have ideally looked for to ensure the safety of all contributors".

But she added that she "completely understood" why Dogra "decided that she doesn't want to proceed with it".

Shona Manderson appeared on the 2023 series of Married at First Sight UK

The other part of the review, by law firm Clyde & Co, found that Channel 4 and CPL's welfare protocols were compliant with Ofcom's broadcasting code.

There were no findings of a breach of the code regarding the handling of issues raised at the relevant times.

But it said there were "a small number of instances" where the show's protocols had not been fully applied.

This included one incident when "some contributors contravened the Code of Conduct relating to prohibited substances but were given a first and final warning rather than being removed from the programme".

It added that Channel 4 and CPL could have undertaken a more structured longer-term review over multiple series.

The review also made recommendations for areas where the contributor welfare framework could be "further strengthened".

Dogra said welfare across all of their programmes is "a primary concern".

She said that considering the "wholesale implementation" of the recommendations "provoked fundamental questions about the editorial proposition of a show that, I believe, has now run its course over 10 years".

She added that the review "did not have the authority to adjudicate on the very serious allegations made by three women in the Panorama programme".

Billed as a "bold social experiment", Married at First Sight UK - known to many as MAFS - sees single people agree to "marry" total strangers, after meeting for the first time at their mock weddings.

The marriages are not legally binding, but viewers see the couples go on honeymoon, before moving in together and navigating their relationships - all while being filmed, almost every day.

The UK version, which had been running for 10 seasons, is one of Channel 4's biggest shows, with audience figures often topping three million.

Following the Panorama broadcast, Channel 4's chief executive Priya Dogra initially didn't apologise, although she did express her "sympathy" for those who had spoken up.

Less than 48 hours later, she changed position, telling reporters she was "deeply sorry" over the women's distress.

The impact of the Panorama progamme was swift, and sizeable.

Channel 4 launched its external review, all the episodes were taken down from its streaming service, and a major sponsor pulled out .

Married at First Sight UK usually starts airing in September, but the new series was put on hold following the revelations in the Panorama.

Ofcom has since launched an investigation, and in June, a male cast member was arrested on suspicion of rape .

The individual is not being named. The alleged victim is also not being named; anyone who makes an allegation of rape is entitled to anonymity by law.

If you have more information about this story, you can reach Noor by email at noor.nanji@bbc.co.uk

Panorama investigates allegations that raise serious concerns that welfare procedures on Married at First Sight UK have failed contributors, leaving them at risk of harm.

I Kigali, inzu ndende zanyeganyejwe n'uyu mutingito wamaze amasegonda miriongo itatu, maze abakorera mu nzu basiganwaa basohoka ngo bahunge icyago bumvaga gishaka kubagwirira.

Uyu mutingito urangiye, biruhukije imitima ko barokotse.

Urwego rw’Igihugu rushinzwe Mine, Peteroli na Gaz (RMB), rwatangaje ko uyu mutingito wari ufite ubukana bwa 6.4, ariko ngo kugeza ubu nta bikorwa byigeze bigaragara waba wangije.

RMB yasobanuye ko uyu mutingito waturutse hafi ya Ushirombo muri Tanzania, mu ntera y’ibilometero 292 uvuye i Kigali.

Ubundi, ubukana bwa 6.4 ngo ntibuhora butera iyangirika ringana. Uburyo umutingito wangiza biterwa n’ubujyakuzimu bwawo, aho wabereye, imiterere y’ubutaka n’ubwiza bw’inyubako.

Mu 2023, umutingito w'ubukana nk'ubwo wabaye muri Turkiya ugwisha amazu icumi, uhitana abantu batandatu, abandi cumi n'umunani barakomereka.

Aha ngaha, ngo hari hashize iminsi habaye undi mutingito, wasize inzu zazahaye, nuko uwakurikiyeho uje urazisonga.

MN202611_8jpy2sanfm.t:
KIGALI – Ten years after the world agreed in Rwanda to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), implementation remains a challenge for people whose livelihoods, healthcare and economic opportunities depend on access to reliable cooling.

Farmers struggle to preserve their harvests, health facilities require dependable refrigeration for vaccines and essential medicines, access to cooling facilities remains a challenge, particularly in Africa, where electricity supply is still limited or unreliable in many communities.

During a high-level segment of the 38th Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol (MOP38) on November 5, Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva highlighted this gap and challenged countries to address it.

The Kigali Amendment is seen as a major international environmental breakthrough, committing to gradually reduce the production and consumption these powerful greenhouse gases widely used in refrigeration and air conditioning.

However, PM Nsengiyumva suggests that the achievement should not become a reason for complacency, saying the next phase must demonstrate that global environmental cooperation can deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives.

“That means this transition must go beyond replacing one technology with another. It must also build the infrastructure, develop the skills and nurture the industries that enable countries to fully benefit from sustainable cooling,” he said.

For farmers, he explained, reliable cold storage can determine whether produce reaches the market or is lost after an entire season’s labor. In healthcare, it can mean ensuring that life-saving vaccines and essential medicines reach even the most remote communities.

For developing countries, this presents a particularly important challenge of expanding access to cooling while ensuring that the technologies supporting that expansion do not undermine efforts to address climate change.

Rwanda seeks to contribute to that effort through the Africa Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Cooling and Cold-chain (ACES), established with a pan-African vision to bring together research, training, technology development and practical application.

Nsengiyumva also called for stronger South-South cooperation and international partnerships, calling for developing countries to have the expertise and resources to shape the transition rather than simply adapt to technologies developed elsewhere.

Elizabeth Maruma Mrema, Deputy Executive Director of the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP), said the Montreal Protocol remains an example of what countries can accomplish through sustained international cooperation.

“Even as reaching global consensus becomes increasingly difficult, the Multilateral Fund, which has supported governments in establishing reporting systems, strengthening regulatory frameworks and building the capacity needed to implement the Kigali Amendment,” she said.

The Multilateral Fund has also supported 127 developing countries in strengthening their capacity to collect, transport and manage used and unwanted controlled substances.

At least 91 Stage I Kigali HFC implementation plans have been approved, with the investments expected to help avoid more than 78 million tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions.

The progress, she said, demonstrates that environmental commitments can translate into practical interventions, but sustaining those gains will require continued investment and stronger national institutions.

“Continued progress will depend on strengthening implementation, building and enhancing institutional capacity, and ensuring that developing countries receive the support they need to meet their commitments,” Mrema said.

One of the major issues before MOP38 is the replenishment of the Multilateral Fund for the 2027–2029 period, which will determine the resources available to support developing countries in meeting their obligations.

Mrema expressed hope that the negotiations would produce adequate financing to sustain implementation of the Kigali Amendment while promoting sustainable cooling over the long term.

Turning a Global Agreement into Local Capacity

The financial discussions come against a broader question of how countries can maintain the spirit of cooperation that made the Montreal Protocol possible in the first place.

Paul Kranjiki, the outgoing President of MOP37, acknowledged that several important issues remained under discussion as the meeting progressed, expressing hope that delegates would resolve them through consensus.

“It is my sincere hope that we will reach agreement on these issues in the spirit of trust and mutual understanding. There is need to maintain collective commitment as countries negotiate the resources and institutional arrangements needed to implement the treaty,” he said.

Delegates were urged not to allow the celebration of past achievements overshadow the work ahead, with a reminder that the Protocol’s success has depended on countries remaining committed to a common purpose.

MOP38 has provided an opportunity to bring the international community back to the question that gave the Kigali Amendment its significance ten years ago on how global environmental cooperation can address a shared problem.

Moving forward, in addition to reducing harmful refrigerants, there is demand for the investment, technology, skills and partnerships that allow communities and economies to benefit from cleaner cooling.

Success for the next decade will be determined not only in the emissions prevented, but also in how far its benefits extend to people and countries that still lack access to reliable cooling.
