MN202611_13vjt71cpnv.t:
Kanya King famously remortgaged her London home to fund the inaugural Mobo awards in 1996

A commemorative stone is to be laid in London in honour of the late Mobo founder Kanya King, to mark the 30th anniversary of the music ceremony.

The Mobo awards music ceremony - which celebrates black music, culture and excellence from the UK and abroad - was launched by King in 1996.

Through Mobo, King is credited with playing a major role in bringing black music and culture to the mainstream in the UK. King died this summer from colon cancer at the age of 57.

The Paving the Way stone will be unveiled on 18 November at her former school, Queens Park Community School in Queen's Park, north-west London.

King posing with Idris Elba, the recipient of the Mobo Inspiration Award in 2014

King was awarded a CBE in 2018 for her contributions to music and culture.

A BBC programme to mark the 30th anniversary, presented by DJ Target, will take viewers through some of the most defining moments, performances, and cultural milestones from the Mobo stage since it was first founded.

The programme, MOBO 30: Iconic Moments , will air on 11 November on BBC One and iPlayer.

The anniversary celebrations will also see V&A East Storehouse present a special temporary display featuring a selection of memorabilia from the Mobo archive.

MN202611_uih76driib.t:
Abanyapolitiki batavuga rumwe n’ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, bibumbiye mu ihuriro C64, batangaje ko bateganya kujya mu Mujyi wa Goma guhura n’uwahoze ari Perezida w’iki gihugu, Joseph Kabila ubu uyoboye Umutwe wa politiki n’igisirikare wa Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), mu rwego rwo gushaka igisubizo cy’ibibazo bya politiki n’umutekano biri mu gihugu.

Ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa bwavuze ko butemera ko abanyapolitiki bajya mu bice bufata nk’ibigenzurwa n’umwanzi.

Mu kiganiro Moïse Katumbi yagiranye na Jeune Afrique yemeje ko ateganya kujya i Goma ari kumwe na Augustin Matata Ponyo, kugira ngo bahure na Joseph Kabila, uri muri uwo mujyi umaze igihe ugenzurwa n’umutwe wa FRN wasimbuye AFC/M23.

Katumbi yavuze ko kuba Kabila ari muri Goma bidakwiye kuba impamvu yatuma batamugenderera, kuko uwo mujyi uri ku butaka bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo kandi Kabila akaba ari Umunye-Congo.

Ati “Tuzajyana i Goma. Goma iri muri Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, Kabila ni Umunye-Congo.”

Yagaragaje ko kuganira na Kabila bidakwiye gufatwa nk’ikibazo, mu gihe ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa na bwo bukomeje kugirana ibiganiro n’uruhande rwa FRN i Doha muri Qatar.

Ati “Guverinoma imwe ya Congo ikomeje kuganira na FRN i Doha.”

Katumbi yavuze ko ihuriro C64 rigizwe n’abanyapolitiki bakomeye barimo Martin Fayulu, Moïse Katumbi, Jean-Marc Kabund, Augustin Matata Ponyo na Delly Sesanga, rihangayikishijwe n’uko guhindura Itegeko Nshinga no gukoresha intwaro mu guhindura ubutegetsi bishobora gukomeza gukururira igihugu ibibazo.

Yagize ati “Tugomba gukora ibishoboka byose kugira ngo tubuze inzira abari i Kinshasa bashaka kurenga ku Itegeko Nshinga n’abafata intwaro, bityo tubashe kubona ubwumvikane binyuze mu mahoro.”

Iri huriro riherutse gutangaza ko ryifuza kuganira na Perezida Félix Tshisekedi ndetse na Joseph Kabila, hagamijwe gushaka igisubizo cy’ibibazo bya politiki n’umutekano byugarije Congo.

Katumbi yasobanuye ko abanyamuryango ba C64 bari i Kinshasa ari bo bazahura na Tshisekedi, mu gihe we na Matata Ponyo, bari mu buhungiro, bateganya kujya i Goma.

Ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa bwavuze ko butemera ko abanyapolitiki bajya mu bice bufata nk’ibigenzurwa n’umwanzi batabiherewe uburenganzira.

Visi Minisitiri w’Intebe akaba na Minisitiri w’Umutekano w’Imbere mu Gihugu, Jacquemain Shabani, yabwiye Jeune Afrique ko nta munyapolitiki ukwiye kujya mu bice nk’ibyo agiye guhura n’ababirimo, atabanje kubiherwa uburenganzira na Guverinoma ya Kinshasa.

Shabani yavuze ko na Joseph Kabila ubwo yajyaga iGoma yavugaga ko agiye kuganira n’ihuriro AFC/M23, birangire ashinze FRN.

Ati “Ndagira ngo mbibutse ko uwahoze ari Perezida yagiye i Goma avuga ko agiye kuganira. Nyuma yerekana uruhare rwe.”

Yavuze ko ibyo byatumye Leta itizera ko abandi banyapolitiki bajya muri ibyo bice bagamije ibiganiro gusa, bityo ko abazarenga kuri ayo mabwiriza bashobora gukurikiranwa hakurikijwe amategeko ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo.

MN202611_15s0tg8tpx2.t:
"Search elsewhere" was the message for the bosses at Google

Protesters claim Google's headquarters in London refused a petition of 54,000 signatories worried about the environmental impact of an Essex development.

The tech giant plans to build four data centre buildings, covering 130,500 sqm, and an office building on the former Arena Essex Raceway near Purfleet which closed in 2018 .

The 52 hectares of land became a Local Wildlife Site in 2006 and conservationists said the development would threaten rare bumblebees and endangered broad-leaved cudweed.

Google would not confirm or deny that it refused the petition on Wednesday, but said data centres were "vital" and that the firm was taking its environmental responsibilities "very seriously".

A number of environmental groups claim the development would wipe out more than 80% of its protected habitats, as the site is also home to butterflies and nightingales.

They have called for Google to "search elsewhere", and want it opened up as a green space and the return of the racers.

Jamie Robins, programmes manager at Buglife, said the plan "makes a mockery" of Google's sustainability claims.

"Handing in this petition today is making it clear to Google that their Thurrock Data Centre plans are inappropriate and unwanted," he said.

"During a nature and climate emergency, with our insects in decline, we should be protecting our precious wildlife sites and need powerful companies to lead and make better decisions."

Emily Buttress, of Essex Wildlife Trust, said: "Its loss would be devastating for the local area.

"It would fragment the ecological network even further, putting already at-risk wildlife under an even greater threat."

A Google spokesperson said: "Data centres are vital to the UK, providing the critical infrastructure required to power our digital economy and the online services used by people in every corner of the UK.

"As we work to deliver this critical infrastructure, we share the Essex Wildlife Trust and Buglife's view that development at the former Arena Essex site must be sustainable.

"Our goal is to regenerate the site, bringing long-term investment and jobs to Thurrock while taking our environmental responsibilities very seriously.

"We are working closely with Natural England and ecological experts to guarantee a 10% Biodiversity Net Gain.

"Our proposal also ensures a substantial part of the site is preserved for new public open space, green links, retained habitat, and the long-term enhancement of key woodland corridors."

MN202611_2dqcy1nbdz.t:
Cetirizine is commonly used to relieve allergy symptoms

Kenyan pharmacists have warned women against inserting allergy tablets into their vaginas in an attempt to make them tighter, following the spread of potentially dangerous medical advice on social media.

The warning follows a wave of social media posts promoting cetirizine - a widely available oral antihistamine used to treat allergies - as a way of tightening the vagina, supposedly to enhance sexual pleasure.

Although antihistamines can sometimes cause dryness as a side effect, experts say this does not strengthen vaginal muscles.

"Dryness is not tightness... instead, it may increase friction, discomfort, and the risk of tissue injury," the Pharmaceutical Society of Kenya (PSK) said.

"Inserting oral tablets is unsafe. Cetirizine tablets are made to be swallowed. Their ingredients have not been tested on delicate vaginal tissue," it added.

Cetirizine is commonly used to relieve symptoms such as sneezing, a runny nose, itchy eyes and skin reactions, including hives.

The controversy began earlier this week when posts circulated on TikTok claiming that cetirizine could reduce vaginal moisture and create a sensation of tightness during sex.

This sparked widespread debate, with some users promoting the practice while others questioned its safety.

There have also been local media reports of the price of the drug rising and increased demand in some pharmacies, especially in the capital, Nairobi.

"Cetirizine is an allergy medicine, taken by mouth. It is not approved or tested for any other purpose, and definitely not for vaginal use," the PSK, a professional body representing pharmacists in Kenya, said in a statement issued on Thursday.

"If you have already tried it. Stop. See a doctor if you have pain, bleeding, burning, itching, unusual discharge, or fever," it advised.

The society also urged social media influencers and content creators to take care when sharing health information, saying that unverified claims could put people's health at risk.

The warning comes a day after Kenya's health ministry expressed concern about the trend.

Ouma Oluga, a senior health official, said some social media users appeared to be treating the medical advice from experts as a joke, without considering the possible consequences.

He suggested that the authorities could introduce a system to track the distribution and purchase of medicines to help identify possible misuse.

However, no formal decision has been announced on such a initiative.

The PSK said it was aware of reports of increased demand for cetirizine, rising prices and shortages at some pharmacies.

It urged retailers not to exploit the trend, warning that people who genuinely needed the medicine for allergies could struggle to obtain it.

It went on to encourage its members not to knowingly dispense medicines that would be misused - and report any side affects to the health authorities of those that had been.

The PSK ended its statement by saying that unverified online trends should never trump what the experts say: "Check with a pharmacist before using any medicine for a purpose it was not made for.

"Do not rely on social media for medical advice."

MN202611_5ojudxb5bn.t:
Cristiano Ronaldo became the first player to win five Champions League trophies and remains the top scorer in the tournament's history

Cristiano Ronaldo says his international career with Portugal is over, meaning the 41-year-old will just play on with Al-Nassr.

The main thing driving him on now is hoping to reach an unprecedented 1,000 career goals - he is currently on 985.

BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of a career that has also taken in spells at Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus.

Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory

Ronaldo will not retire until he scores 1,000 goals

Untouchable or a support act? Ronaldo's 1,000-goal quest continues

Cristiano Ronaldo had one season in the Sporting first team before moving to Old Trafford

After 31 first-team games and five goals for Sporting, Ronaldo caught the eye of Manchester United in a pre-season friendly in 2003, setting up two goals in a 3-1 win in Lisbon.

Ronaldo revealed that United boss Alex Ferguson took him into the dressing room afterwards to meet the players.

Five days later he joined the Red Devils for £12m.

"After we played Sporting the lads in the dressing room talked about him constantly, and on the plane back from the game they urged me to sign him - that's how highly they rated him," said Ferguson.

"He is one of the most exciting young players I've ever seen."

Cristiano Ronaldo has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia

Ronaldo won the FA Cup in his first season at United, scoring in the final against Millwall.

But it was in 2006-07 that his career really exploded. He hit 17 Premier League goals, his first season of double figures, was named player of the year and young player of the year - and won his first league title.

The following season was even better, winning his first Champions League - scoring in the final - his first European Golden Shoe for top scorer, and another league title.

Cristiano Ronaldo won the first Puskas award - and it remains the only Champions League goal to win it

Ronaldo scored 118 goals in 292 games in his first spell at United, and one was ranked above all the others.

He hit an absolute rocket of a shot into the top corner from 40 yards in his homeland against Porto, a goal which took them into the Champions League semi-finals.

It won the inaugural Fifa Puskas award for goal of the year.

Months later, Ronaldo joined Real Madrid for £80m.

Cristiano Ronaldo helped Real Madrid to win their first Copa del Rey in seven years

Ronaldo's first season at Real Madrid produced no trophies and his second saw just the Copa del Rey won.

That final was especially notable because it is the first time Ronaldo had scored the winning goal in a final. And it was in El Clasico, one of four meetings in 18 days in all competitions.

He rose at the far post to power in a trademark header from Angel di Maria's cross in extra time as Real beat Barcelona 1-0.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored 14 goals in 14 games against Levante

Ronaldo, then 30, scored in a 3-0 La Liga win over Levante in October 2015 to become the club's all-time top scorer with his 324th goal in 310 games.

The 2015-16 campaign would go on to be the sixth season in a row that Ronaldo scored 50 or more goals in all competitions.

Ronaldo ended up extending that record by 126 goals - leaving Real with 450 goals in just 438 games.

Cristiano Ronaldo is the top scorer in European Championship history - with 14 goals - as well as lifting the trophy once

The one thing missing from Ronaldo's CV was international success.

And that came in 2016 when Portugal won the European Championship by beating hosts France 1-0 in the final in Paris.

Ronaldo ended up taking on an unofficial coaching role in that final after going off injured in tears midway through the first half.

He was named in the team of the tournament after three goals and three assists. Ronaldo retires as the top scorer in Euros history, with 14 goals.

Cristiano Ronaldo has won five Ballons d'Or, only behind Lionel Messi

Cristiano Ronaldo won his fifth Ballon d'Or, equalling Lionel Messi's record at the time, after winning the Champions League and La Liga in 2016-17. He netted twice in that European final over Juventus.

It followed on from the best player in the world awards in 2008, 2013, 2014 and 2016.

Sadly for Ronaldo, Messi would go on to win three more Ballons d'Or, meaning he won their personal rivalry 8-5.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored one of his eight Champions League hat-tricks in the 2017 win over Bayern Munich

Ronaldo became the first player to score 100 Champions League goals with a hat-trick in the 2016-17 quarter-final second leg win over Bayern Munich.

Only Messi and Robert Lewandowski have joined him to date in the century club.

Ronaldo would go on to score 141 goals in 187 games (also a record) in Europe's top competition. For six seasons in a row he was the tournament's top scorer or joint top scorer.

"That is one of the great goals you will see… I was going to say Champions League football, but, basically, football," said Pat Nevin in BBC Radio 5 Live commentary

In 2018 came one of the most iconic moments of Ronaldo's career, maybe the greatest Champions League goal ever scored.

In the quarter-final, Ronaldo leapt into the air before acrobatically firing into the corner of the net with an incredible bicycle kick against Juventus.

Even the Juve fans stood up to applaud the player who would join their club months later.

It was nominated for the Puskas Award but he finished second to Mohamed Salah's goal for Liverpool against Everton.

The night Juventus rose to applaud Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo was the first man to win five Champions Leagues, although he was not the last as Real Madrid kept winning it without him

Ronaldo won two La Liga titles and two Copa del Rey trophies at Real Madrid, but it was in Europe's elite club competition where he became a true legend.

He had already won the Champions League in 2008 with United, and went on to win it four more times with Real.

The first was in 2014 before a remarkable three times in a row in 2016, 2017 and 2018 (beating Liverpool in the Gareth Bale/Loris Karius final) to become the first player to win the Champions League five times.

Since his departure, former Real team-mates Toni Kroos, Dani Carvajal, Luka Modric and Nacho have gone on to win six.

Cristiano Ronaldo had a penalty saved by Gavin Bazunu before netting twice to deny Ireland a famous win in Faro

Ali Daei scored 109 goals for Iran between 1993 and 2006 - and it was felt like maybe his world record for international goals in men's football would never be broken.

But Ronaldo's two late headers in a World Cup qualifying win over the Republic of Ireland in 2021 took him onto 111 goals.

He kept adding to that total and finished on 146 goals in 234 caps - also a record for international appearances.

Cristiano Ronaldo was the first player in professional football to ever hit 900 official goals

Ronaldo continued to smash the goals in for Juventus, in his second spell at United and at Al-Nassr but failed to really replicate many truly magic moments of the past.

However he did create some history in 2024 as he became the first player to score 900 top-level career goals as Portugal beat Croatia.

That number is now 985 - so he is only 15 off an unprecedented 1,000th goal.

He has now hit five for Sporting, 450 for Real Madrid, 145 for Manchester United, 101 for Juventus, 138 for Al-Nassr and 146 for Portugal.

He recently confirmed that he is aiming to hit the 1,000 mark.

But old rival Messi is on 931 goals, the second highest scorer ever, so Ronaldo cannot afford to dawdle too much...

MN202611_wgl1cqdxtk.t:
Noah Wyle stars in The Pitt, the medical series set in a Pittsburgh emergency room that first aired in 2025

US drama The Pitt is similar enough to medical series ER for a lawsuit against its producers to progress, a court in the US has ruled.

The widow of Michael Crichton, who created ER, argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the series, which has been made without proper permission or credit.

Sherri Crichton says her husband's contract included a "frozen rights" provision that prohibited any spin-offs, sequels or reboots of ER being made without his express consent.

A three-judge panel said there are "clear and numerous similarities between The Pitt and ER," which means the case can go ahead. Warner Bros previously described the lawsuit as "baseless" and sought to have it dismissed.

Listing the similarities between the two shows, the court cited the emergency room setting, the fast pace, use of medical jargon, graphic depictions of injuries, and younger doctors fresh from medical school being trained.

"We find the details here suffice for a prima facie case," the judges said.

It means the case will now go to a jury trial in Los Angeles Superior Court.

But the judges dismissed separate claims against actor-producer Noah Wyle, executive producer John Wells and showrunner R Scott Gemmill.

The justices said there was insufficient evidence to show the three producers were aware they could be violating Crichton's contractual rights.

Noah Wyle (second right) previously starred in ER alongside Anthony Edwards, George Clooney and Eriq La Salle

ER launched in 1994, based on original screenplay written by Crichton. It starred George Clooney, Anthony Edwards, Eriq La Salle and Maria Bello, and aired 331 episodes over the next 15 years.

The show, which followed a group of doctors working in an emergency room in Chicago, was a hit with viewers and critics, and won 23 Emmy Awards during its run including outstanding drama series.

Discussions about a possible reboot of the show began in 2020, and studio Warner Bros spent months negotiating with Crichton's estate.

Those talks were reported to have collapsed over credit and financial guarantees, and producers began developing The Pitt in its place.

But Sherri Crichton and the John Michael Crichton Trust argue the show is a rebranded but uncredited reboot of ER, using the same formula, pacing, style and setting, rather than an entirely original series.

They said producers "simply moved the show from Chicago to Pittsburgh, rebranded it The Pitt, and ploughed ahead without any attribution or compensation for Crichton and his heirs".

Many actors and creatives from ER also work on The Pitt, including Wyle, Gemmill and Wells.

After legal action began in 2024, Warner Bros Television said in a statement that the lawsuit was "baseless", arguing that The Pitt was a "new and original show", adding that the studio would "vigorously defend against these meritless claims".

But in a 33-page opinion published on Wednesday, a three-judge panel unanimously upheld an earlier ruling that Crichton's estate had presented enough evidence to pursue its claim.

Warner Bros had sought to have the lawsuit dismissed on appeal, arguing the shows shared only "generic similarities" common to "any dramatic story involving emergency room doctors".

The judges said they had compared the opening episode scripts for the two shows and found sufficient similarities in plot, themes, dialogue, mood, setting, pace, characters, graphic injury detail and sequence of events.

Sherri Crichton said: "I am deeply gratified by the Court of Appeal decision and look forward to discovery and to our case, which affects writers, creators, and their families and estates, being presented to a jury."

Warner Bros has not yet commented on the latest ruling.

MN202611_1jn7146yyis.t:
Jesus Owono helped Equatorial Guinea to the quarter-finals of the 2021 Afcon but the National Thunder suffered a group-stage exit at the 2025 finals in Morocco

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono will miss Equatorial Guinea's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifiers this month following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

Owono said he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" in a statement issued by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, adding that it is "very hard to come to terms with what has happened".

Equatorial Guinea's football federation (Feguifut) said that the 25-year-old had requested to be left out of coach Vincenzo Alberto Annese's squad.

Feguifut president Venancio Tomas Micha had previously said his organisation was offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.

Owono has been first-choice keeper for the National Thunder since November 2020 and has featured at the past three Afcons.

Equatorial Guinea face Zimbabwe in a double-header in Group E, with a home match in Bata on Thursday, 12 November before a trip to Harare four days later.

The two teams sit level on three points after two rounds of matches, with DR Congo top of the standings on six points and Sierra Leone pointless at the bottom of the table.

MN202611_w6mftm756g.t:
Minisitiri w’Intebe w’u Rwanda, Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva, yasabye ibihugu gushyira imbaraga mu gushyira mu bikorwa amasezerano mpuzamahanga agamije kurengera ikirere, ashimangira ko intambwe imaze guterwa idakwiye gutuma Isi inyurwa n’ibyagezweho, ahubwo ko hakenewe ibikorwa bifatika birushijeho.

Yabigarutseho ku wa 5 Ugushyingo 2026, ubwo yayoboraga umuhango wo gutangiza ku mugaragaro Inama ya 38 ihuza ibihugu byasinye Amasezerano ya Montreal agamije kurengera akayunguruzo k’imirasire y’izuba, izwi nka MOP38, iri kubera i Kigali.

Minisitiri w’Intebe yavuze ko u Rwanda rwishimiye kwakira iyi nama, agaragaza ko ifite igisobanuro cyihariye kuko nyuma y’imyaka 10 ari bwo Kigali yongeye kwakira inama ihuriza hamwe ibihugu mu biganiro bigamije kurengera ibidukikije.

Yibukije ko mu myaka 10 ishize, Kigali yabaye umujyi wahurije hamwe ibihugu byiyemeje kugabanya ikoreshwa ry’imyuka ya ‘Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs),’ binyuze mu ivugururwa ry’Amasezerano ya Montreal ryiswe ‘Kigali Amendment’.

Yavuze ko ayo masezerano yagaragaje ko ibihugu bishobora gufatanya guhangana n’ibibazo byugarije isi, by’umwihariko ibijyanye n’imihindagurikire y’ikirere, byita ku nzego zitandukanye z’iterambere ryabyo.

Ati “Byanagaragaje impamvu Amasezerano ya Montreal amaze igihe kirekire yubahirizwa: ubushobozi bwayo bwo guhangana n’ibibazo bishya, kubakira ku byagezweho no gukomeza ibikorwa bihuriweho.”

Yakomeje avuga ko ishyirwa mu bikorwa ryuzuye ry’ivugururwa ry’Amasezerano ya Kigali rizagira uruhare rukomeye mu kurengera ikirere no guteza imbere imibereho myiza y’abatuye isi, ubu n’abazaza..

Yatanze urugero ku kamaro ko gukoresha ikoranabuhanga rikonjesha , agaragaza ko gukonjesha ibiribwa ku bahinzi bisobanuye , kubona uburyo bwo kubika umusaruro mu bukonje bushobora gutuma ibyo bejeje bigera ku isoko bitangiritse, mu gihe ku bakozi bo mu rwego rw’ubuzima bifasha kubika inkingo n’imiti bikenewe mu kurokora ubuzima bw’abaturage, harimo n’abatuye mu bice bya kure.

Ati “ Hejuru y’ako kamaro kose, uburyo bwiza bwo gukonjesha ntiburagera ku baturage amamiliyoni by’umwihariko muri Afurika, aho amashanyarazi akiri make cyangwa ataboneka mu buryo buhoraho.”

Yavuze ko uko abantu bakenera gukonjesha ibintu bagenda biyongera, ibihugu bikwiye gushaka ibisubizo birengera ikirere, bikoresha ingufu neza kandi bigendana na gahunda zo kugeza amashanyarazi ku baturage, kongera ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ikirere no guteza imbere ubukungu.

Yavuze kandi ko nta gihugu gishobora kugera kuri iyo ntego cyonyine, ashimangira akamaro k’ubufatanye hagati y’ibihugu bikiri mu nzira y’amajyambere ndetse n’ibindi bihugu n’imiryango mpuzamahanga.

Ati “Ubufatanye nk’ubwo ni ingenzi kugira ngo ibihugu bikiri mu nzira y’amajyambere bigire uruhare rwuzuye mu gushyiraho no kuyobora izi mpinduka, aho gutegerezwa gusa kuzimenyera.”

Minisitiri w’Intebe yasabye ibihugu kudahagarara ku byo bisabwa n’amasezerano mpuzamahanga, ahubwo bigaharanira kugera ku musaruro urenze ibisabwa, birimo gushyira mu bikorwa ibyo byiyemeje ku gihe no gushora imari mu bikorwa remezo n’ikoranabuhanga rirengera ikirere.

MN202611_1xem8v4f5by.t:
The company said it was beginning a "new chapter"

A Newport aviation company, that has grown into a global supplier of aircraft engines, parts and maintenance services, has been bought in a deal worth about £475m.

Japanese firm ORIX Aviation has agreed to acquire AerFin, which employs more than 230 people and operates from sites in the UK and around the world.

Founded by Bob James, AerFin has developed from a south Wales business into a global aviation aftermarket specialist.

Announcing the takeover, AerFin described it as the start of a new chapter for the company.

The firm - which was majority owned by a private equity company prior to the sale - buys, sells, leases and repairs aircraft, engines and components.

In 2025, the company moved into a new purpose-built, 116,000 sq ft facility , external at Indurent Park in Newport.

There are no plans to move its headquarters from Newport.

ORIX Aviation is the aircraft leasing arm of Japanese financial services giant the ORIX Group.

Simon Goodson, AerFin's chief executive, said the deal would help grow the business

Chief executive Simon Goodson called the acquisition a "defining moment" in the company's history.

"I am delighted that AerFin is joining the ORIX Group, a business that shares our values and belief in trusted partnerships, flexible solutions and finding the way ahead for our customers," he said.

He said support from the wider ORIX Group would provide "the confidence and platform" to grow the aviation business.

"This is a defining moment in AerFin's story and the beginning of an exciting new chapter," said Goodson.

Aerfin helps airlines and aviation companies source parts and manage assets

AerFin has built its existing business around extending the life of aircraft and engines through trading, leasing, repair and reuse.

It helps airlines and aviation companies source parts and manage assets. The company claims to serve more than 600 organisations.

AerFin moved into a new purpose-built facility in Newport last year

For ORIX Aviation, the acquisition expands its activities beyond aircraft ownership and leasing, into aftermarket services and end-of-life aircraft management.

The company said the combination would strengthen its capabilities across the entire lifecycle of an aircraft.

James Meyler, chief executive of ORIX Aviation, said AerFin had built "a leading aviation aftermarket platform" supported by extensive technical expertise and an international customer base.

The sale also marks the exit of Danish private equity investor CataCap, which had been the majority shareholder in AerFin.

Founder Bob James said he was pleased to see the business move to what he described as "a long-term home", capable of supporting AerFin's next phase of expansion.

"I recognise a strong leadership team and a long-term home when I see one," James said.

MN202611_1bpz88uq5gc.t:
Kuri uyu wa Kane, Cristiano Ronaldo w'imyaka 41 y'amavuko yatangaje ko asezeye mu ikipe y'igihugu ya Portugal nyuma y'imyaka 23 ayikiniye bwa mbere, mu gihe asize ayikiniye imikino 234. Ibi icyamamare mu mupira w'amaguru ku Isi, Cristiano Ronaldo, yabitangaje abinyujije ku mbugankoranyambaga ze asoza urugendo rw'imyaka 23 yaranzwe n'amateka akomeye, ibikombe n'ibihembo bitandukanye akinira ikipe y'igihugu ya Portugal.

Mu mashusho maremare yashyize ku rubuga rwa Instagram, yasomeye abakunzi be ibaruwa ibamenyesha ko igihe kigeze ngo asezere mu ikipe y'igihugu.

Mu magambo ye, Ronaldo yagize ati: “Umunsi wageze ngo nsubize nimero 7 y'ikipe y'igihugu cyacu. Sinigeze ntekereza ko yari iyange njyenyine gusa, ariko mu gihe cy'imyaka 23 nagize amahirwe n'inshingano byo kuyambara.”

Ronaldo asize amateka akomeye mu ikipe y'Igihugu ya Portugal, aho yayikiniye imikino 234, ayitsindira ibitego 146. Iyi mibare imugira umukinnyi wakiniye igihugu cye imikino myinshi ndetse akanagitsindira ibitego byinshi mu mateka y'umupira w'amaguru ku rwego rw'ibihugu.

Yatangiye gukinira Portugal mu 2003, ubwo yari afite imyaka 18, kuva icyo gihe aba umwe mu bakinnyi b'ingenzi mu rugendo rw'iyi kipe mu marushanwa akomeye ku Isi.

Mu byo azahora yibukirwaho harimo gufasha Portugal kwegukana igikombe cya UEFA Euro 2016, nyuma yo gutsinda u Bufaransa ku mukino wa nyuma, ndetse no kwegukana UEFA Nations League mu 2019 no mu 2025.

Yitabiriye ibikombe bitandatu by'Isi, kuva mu 2006 kugeza mu 2026, aba umwe mu bakinnyi bake cyane bageze kuri ayo mateka. Yanasize izina rikomeye mu marushanwa ya UEFA European Championship, aho yabaye umukinnyi watsinze ibitego byinshi mu mateka yayo.

Kuva mu 2003 kugeza mu 2026, Ronaldo yagaragaje ubudasa mu ikipe y'igihugu, aho imyaka myinshi yayibereye kapiteni, ayobora bagenzi be kandi akomeza kuba intwaro ikomeye mu busatirizi.

Kuva ubu, Portugal igiye gukomeza urugendo rwayo idafite umukinnyi wari umaze imyaka irenga makumyabiri ari isura yayo mu mupira w'amaguru.

Italian chef Davide Tamburella was fired from a Brisbane restaurant in May after the establishment's management expressed concerns about a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour.

Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function.

It was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years.

At the time, the chef had stated that putting pineapple on pizza was "offensive to his culture".

MN202611_qmgfzu8deg.t:
Leah Williamson, Beth Mead and Mary Fowler have all experienced ACL injuries

The Football Association and WSL Football have launched a major research project to better understand why anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries occur in women's football and identify ways to reduce them.

Funded by the FA, the PhD study with Imperial College London and sports knee surgeon Simon Ball will be led by researcher Hanna Lehtovirta and involve clubs across the Women's Super League and WSL2.

ACL injuries are among the most serious issues facing the women's game, often keeping players out for months.

Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer the injury than their male counterparts.

Vivianne Miedema, Beth Mead, Leah Williamson and Sam Kerr are among the players to have suffered the injury over recent years.

While previous studies have highlighted potential risk factors including anatomical, hormonal, biomechanical and environmental influences, researchers say less is known about how those factors interact in the day-to-day experience of elite football.

The study aims to provide one of the most comprehensive examinations of ACL injuries in women's football by combining scientific data with the experiences of players and staff.

Players from every WSL and WSL2 club will be invited to take part, alongside medical, performance and coaching staff.

The research will be conducted in two phases.

The first will use player surveys to gather data on injury history, training and match load, and hormonal, nutritional and psychological factors.

Data from players who have suffered ACL injuries since 2018-19 will be compared with those who have not.

The second phase will involve interviews with players and staff to explore perceptions of ACL injuries and current approaches to training and prevention.

Researchers hope the findings will help shape future injury prevention, rehabilitation and player welfare strategies in the women's game.

In April 2025, Fifa announced they were also funding research into whether hormonal fluctuations during menstrual cycles could be contributing to the rise in ACL injuries in women's football.

MN202611_4699cjoq29.t:
Bamwe mu bagabo bo mu Karere ka Nyabihu bavuga ko bakubitwa ndetse bakanatukwa n’abagore babo, ariko bakaryumaho kubera gutinya gusekwa, gusuzugurwa cyangwa kutitabwaho mu gihe bagaragaje ihohoterwa bakorerwa.

Ihohoterwa rikorerwa abagabo muri aka Karere ryavuye kuri 16,8% mu 2019/2020 rigera kuri 26% mu 2025, nk’uko bigaragazwa n’ubushakashatsi bwa karindwi ku Mibereho n’Ubuzima (RDHS7).

Bamwe mu bagabo bo muri Nyabihu bavuga ko iyo amakimbirane akaze, bahitamo kuva mu ngo zabo bakajya gucumbika ahandi, aho kwihimura ku bagore babo cyangwa gukora ibindi byabakururira kujya imbere y’amategeko.

Manizabayo Moussa, utuye mu Murenge wa Jenda, yabwiye UMUSEKE ko hari abagabo azi bahozwa ku nkoni n’abagore babo, ariko bakabihisha abandi, bamwe bakabeshya ko ibikomere bagize byatewe no kwikubita hasi.

Ati: “Hari umugabo uherutse kuvuga ikibazo afite, umugore we aramuseka amugereranya n’imbwa. Hari n’abo usanga baraye bakubiswe, ariko ntibatinyuke kujya kurega. Benshi bashirira imbere.”

Yavuze ko bamwe batinya gutanga ibirego kuko bumva ko kuvuga ko bakubiswe n’abagore babo ari igisebo mu bandi.

Ati: “Urya inkoni ukicecekera, kuko uba utinya ko abandi baguseka.”

Undi mugabo ufite umugore n’abana babiri avuga ko ahora afite impungenge zo gutaha, bitewe n’amakimbirane akomoka ku bibazo by’amikoro yo mu rugo.

Ati: “Ntaha mu rugo nigengesereye, nk’aho ngiye gupfukama. Ubu nabuze akazi, nshobora kugera mu rugo umugore akansaba amafaranga. Namubwira ko ntayo nabonye akavuga ko nayajyanye mu bagore, akankubita.”

Uyu mugabo avuga ko nubwo hari igihe umugore we amukubita, ahitamo kutamukoraho kuko atinya ko yafungwa.

Ati: “Amaboko yanjye aba asa n’uyafatiye inyuma. Ndemera nkihangana aho kurwana nawe.”

Yongeyeho ko hari abagore bafashe nabi ihame ry’uburinganire, bakumva ko ribemerera gusuzugura abagabo babo, bityo abagabo bagahitamo guceceka batinya gufungwa cyangwa guseba.

Nyiramajeri Jacqueline na we avuga ko hari abagore batubaha abo bashakanye, bamwe bakajya mu tubari bagataha batonganya cyangwa bagakubita abagabo babo.

Ati: “Ugasanga umugabo ni we uteka, umugore akamuhemba kumukubita. Abahungu bacu baragowe, bagire batabarwe.”

Yasabye ko hakorwa ubukangurambaga bufasha abashakanye gusobanukirwa ihame ry’uburinganire no kubahana, aho kurifata nk’urwitwazo rwo guhohotera abo bashakanye.

Guverineri w’Intara y’Iburengerazuba, Ntibitura Jean Bosco, avuga ko izamuka ry’imibare y’abagabo bagaragaza ko bahohoterwa ridakwiye guhita risobanurwa nk’izamuka ry’ihohoterwa ubwaryo, kuko rishobora guterwa n’uko abagabo barushijeho gutinyuka kuvuga ibibabaho.

Ati: “Ntabwo mvuga ko byiyongereye kubera ko abagore bagize amahane kurushaho, ahubwo bishobora kuba ari uko abagabo batangiye kubigaragaza. Ubu amakuru arihuta, bityo ikitaramenyekanaga kera kikaba kimenyekana.”

Yungamo ko : “Nta muntu n’umwe wemerewe guhohotera undi, yaba umugore, yaba umugabo, yaba ababyeyi bahohotera abana.”

Ubushakashatsi bwa Rwanda DHS7 bwo mu 2025 bugaragaza ko abagabo bahuye n’ihohoterwa rikorerwa mu ngo biyongereye bava kuri 12,5% bagera kuri 17,2%, mu gihe ku bagore byagabanutseho 0,5%.

Mu Ntara y’Iburengerazuba, igipimo cy’abagabo bahuye n’ihohoterwa cyavuye kuri 14,2% kigera kuri 20,5%, mu gihe mu Ntara y’Amajyepfo cyazamutse kivuye kuri 13,1% kigera kuri 19,4%.

Imibare NISR yatangaje mu 2025 igaragaza ko mu 2024, abagabo 3.233 bagejejwe kuri Isange One Stop Centre nyuma yo gukorerwa ihohoterwa, biyongereye ugereranyije n’abagabo 3.214 bari bahagejejwe mu 2023.

MN202611_d39na71khp.t:
Rwanda’s central bank governor, Soraya Hakuziyaremye, has received the 2026 African Woman in Finance Award, recognising her leadership and contribution to the development of Africa’s financial sector.

The award, presented by the Africa Financial Summit (AFIS), was given to Hakuziyaremye at a ceremony in Luanda, Angola, on November 3.

It recognises women with strong professional records who have helped lead financial institutions, shape policy and expand access to financial services, particularly for underserved communities.

Hakuziyaremye became the first woman to lead the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) when she was appointed governor in February 2025. She had served as deputy governor since March 2021.

Before joining the central bank, she was Minister of Trade and Industry from 2018 to 2021. During that period, she contributed to the implementation of the Made in Rwanda policy and took part in work supporting the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

AFIS said Rwanda’s industries recorded average annual growth of 9% during her tenure, while exports also increased.

Hakuziyaremye has also worked to advance women’s participation in finance and economic development. She was a member of the Graça Machel Trust’s expert group on women’s financial inclusion and, in September 2025, became the first woman to chair the board of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion (AFI).

The award highlights women’s growing role in financial leadership and the importance of extending financial services beyond higher-income groups to women, young people, farmers and others with limited access.

It also recognises the link between effective financial-sector leadership, economic development and national financial stability.

MN202611_14ah0zjfrrx.t:
Mu itangazo ryashyizwe ahagaragara kuri uyu wa 4 Ugushyingo 2026, Umujyi wa Kigali wavuze ko iki cyemezo gikurikira ubugenzuzi bukomeje gukorwa hagamijwe kureba niba inyubako zubahiriza amabwiriza agenga gukumira no kwirinda inkongi.

Izo nyubako n’ahakorerwa ibikorwa by’ubucuruzi biteganyijwe gufungwa guhera ku wa Gatanu, tariki ya 6 Ugushyingo 2026, saa moya z’umugoroba (19:00), kugira ngo ba nyirazo babanze bashyire mu bikorwa ingamba zikenewe zo gukumira inkongi.

Ahagenewe gufungwa harimo Catchup Building iri ku Gisementi, Agakiriro ka Gatenga, Agakiriro ka Gahanga, Rwanda Foam Showroom iri i Gikondo, KAL Plaza iri Gikondo, N&B Plaza iri Kigarama, Eden Tower, Matheus House, Ntaganzwa House na Ndaru Arcade, byose biri mu Karere ka Nyarugenge.

Umujyi wa Kigali wavuze ko izi ngamba zigamije kurengera ubuzima bw’abakora muri izo nyubako, abazisura n’abahakorera ibikorwa by’ubucuruzi, ndetse no kurinda imitungo yabo ishobora kwangizwa n’inkongi.

Ba nyir’inyubako, abazicunga n’abandi bose bagaragajweho ibitagenda neza mu bijyanye no kwirinda inkongi basabwe kwihutira gukemura ibibazo byagaragaye, bakuzuza ibisabwa n’amabwiriza agenga umutekano w’inyubako.

Ubuyobozi bw’Umujyi wa Kigali bwashimangiye ko inyubako izaba yujuje ibisabwa mu kwirinda inkongi izemererwa kongera gufungura, nyuma y’uko inzego zibishinzwe ziyigenzuye zikemeza ko yujuje ibisabwa.

Bwibukije ba nyir’inyubako n’abazicunga ko bafite inshingano zo guhora bazibungabunga no kubahiriza amabwiriza y’umutekano, kugira ngo ubuzima bw’abazikoreramo, abazigana n’abaturiye aho ziherereye burindwe.

MN202611_1eak2f6cyw0.t:
A second buyer has made a rescue bid for Poundland as the discount retailer teeters on the brink of collapse, with thousands of jobs at risk.

London-based Xyra Group has offered to pay off half of Poundland's outstanding debts - a key sticking point in takeover talks so far - immediately. The rest would be deferred.

With Poundland close to collapse, US-based owners Gordon Brothers have already rejected a rival bid from an Irish property group which would have saved its 12,000 staff.

Gordon Brothers said the business has faced years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable".

Sources familiar with the offer said Xyra is offering to immediately pay off £12.5m of an outstanding £30m loan on Poundland's books.

The offer came as Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds held crunch talks with Gordon Brothers about the future of the business, urging the investment firm to protect staff however possible.

Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, committed at the meeting to prioritise offers which protect its shops and workers.

The company said: "We are pursuing all avenues through the sale process to find a solution which protects as many jobs as possible and preserves value. Work continues at pace, engaging in active discussions on offers with interested parties."

Xyra is offering to pay off a higher proportion of Poundland's outstanding debts than Martin Property Group, which previously submitted a bid that Gordon Brothers rejected.

But doubts remain about the credibility of Xyra's offer, as there is little evidence they meet Gordon Brothers' tests, including whether they have the money and whether they would be good long-term owners of Poundland.

Sources pointed to the appointment of Andrew Brode to Xyra's board as a sign of its credibility. Brode works for RWS - a company that provides AI solutions for businesses.

Judith MacKenzie, head of Downing Fund Managers, told the BBC Brode is "well known and very credible" among small businesses in the UK.

But she said there is "hardly any information" publicly available about Xyra. "So, although some of the people look good, I can't find any evidence to say that they've got the money to back it up yet," MacKenzie added.

Gordon Brothers said: "Our intent throughout the comprehensive sale process has been to protect as many jobs as possible and preserve value in order to deliver the best available outcome for all the people, creditors and local communities who care about this business as much as we do."

Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of Poundland has not yet been made.

Though Xyra made an offer to take over the whole business, it is unclear whether it would keep Poundland together as its owner or break the company up.

Several Poundland suppliers have said they would also go bust if the retailer collapses. Its founder Steve Smith said two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, those who solely work for Poundland, would be caught up in the collapse.

He added that not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall.

Ikarata zitukura 53 – za mbere nyinshi kw'isi – ni zo zatanzwe muri Brésil mu rukino rw'umupira w'amaguru, mw'ihiganwa ry'abatarenza imyaka 20, rwaranzwe n'imishamirano hamwe n'akajagari bikomeye.

Muri urwo rukino rubanza rw'igice ca kabiri gishira ica nyuma rwahuje, ku wa Mungu, imirwi Uberlandia na Mamore mu ntara ya Minas, abakinyi 43 hamwe n'abakozi umunani b'imirwi bo mu gisata co kumenyereza barirukanywe mu kibuga.

Hanabayeko abandi bantu babiri bo mu butegetsi bw'umurwi wa Uberlandia bahawe ikarata, bituma ikarata zose zatanzwe zishika 53.

Imbere y'aho, igitigiri kinini c'ikarata zitukura zari zimaze gutangwa mu rukino rumwe cari 36. Zari zatanzwe mu 2011, mu rukino rw'ihiganwa ryo mu cicaro ca gatanu muri Argentine, rwari rwahuje imirwi ya Club Atletico Claypole na Victoriano Arenas.

Ikimenyeshamakuru co muri Brésil, O Tempo, cavuze ko inzego z'umutekano zahamagawe kubera ibice bitandukanye vy'ikibuga ca Parque do Sabia vyari vyononekaye cane.

Nk'uko bivugwa muri raporo y'umuhagarikizi, mu gice ca kabiri c'urukino harabaye ugutana mu mitwe hagati y'abakinyi, inyuma y'uko umukinyi wa Mamore yitwa Davi asomborokeje, mu gutyoza, abagize umurwi wa Uberlandia bari bicaye ku ntebe y'abasubirizi, mu gihe umurwi wiwe wariko wigina igitsindo ca 3 kuri 1.

Umumenyereza w'abanyezamu ba Uberlandia, Paulo Sergio Dias Dos Santos, yaciye yinjira mu kibuga yiruka aja guhangana na Davi. Ivyo vyatumye haduka imishamirano no kurwana hagati y'abakinyi, bikurikirwa no kwirukanwa kwabo mu kibuga, mu gihe imbere y'aho hari hamaze kwirukanwa abandi bakinyi batatu.

Raporo y'igipolisi ivuga ko imiryango 14 yari yabomowe, ibikoresho vyo mu bwogero birononekara, amadirisha aramenagurika, hamwe n'intebe, amameza n'ibindi bikoresho vyo kwicarako birasamburwa.

Urukino rwabanje guhagarikwa mu kiringo c'iminota hafi 40, imbere y'uko umuhagarikizi Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto afata ingingo yo kuruhagarika burundu.

Inyuma y'ivyo, umurwi Uberlandia watangaje icese ko wemeye ko utsinzwe urukino rwo gusubiriza rw'ico gice ca kabiri gishira ica nyuma, kuko Mamore wari usigaranye abakinyi indwi gusa bashobora gukina, bivuye kw'ikarata zitukura zose zatanzwe.

Uberlandia yavuze ko iyo ngingo ari ikimenyetso c'"ukwubaha no gukurikiza ubutungane" (gesture of fair play), ibizoca bituma Mamore uja mu gice ca nyuma c'ihiganwa, mu gihe Uberlandia wo uzokwitegurira urukino rwo kurondera ikibanza ca gatatu.

Umurwi wa Uberlandia yongeyeko uti: "Umurwi nawo ntiwagumye mu gacerere: ibihano nyavyo bijanye n'inyifato vyerekeye abagize uruhara bija bimaze gufatwa imbere mu murwi, kuko iterambere ry'ubunonotsi, imbere ya vyose, ni ikibazo c'iterambere ry'umuntu ku giti ciwe.''

MN202611_1p0kejb67xx.t:
Gérard Buscher wahoze ari Umuyobozi wa Tekiniki mu Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru mu Rwanda, FERWAFA, [DTN], yagizwe umuyobozi wa Tekiniki [Directeur Technique] muri AS Marsa yo muri Shampiyona y’Icyiciro cya mbere muri Tunisie.

Ni amakuru yamenyekanye kuri uyu wa 5 Ugushyingo 2026, nyuma y’uko ibinyamakuru bitandukanye byo muri iki gihugu bigarutse ku nkuru yemeza ko Buscher yamaze kugirwa Umuyobozi wa Tekiniki muri AS Marsa ikina Shampiyona y’icyiciro cya mbere muri Tunisie.

Gérard ni inshuro ya gatatu asubiye muri iyi kipe nyuma yo kuyibera umutoza mu 2010 kugeza mu 2013 no mu 2015 kugeza mu 2016.

Mbere yo kuva mu Rwanda aho yari amaze imyaka ine, uyu Mufaransa yafashije umupira w’u Rwanda, cyane ko aho ahagereye, amahugurwa atandukanye y’abatoza yiyongereye.

Kimwe mu byo abatoza b’Abanyarwanda bazahora bamwibukiraho, ni uburyo yagize uruhare mu mahugurwa y’Impamyabumenyi ya CAF A y’abatoza nyuma y’imyaka hafi 10 ataba mu Rwanda.

Ubwo yari mu Rwanda kandi, Gérard Buscher yagize uruhare mu bwiyongere bwa za license B-CAF ndetse na C-CAF.

MN202611_jhvg74ocny.t:
The film adapts the revered Hindu epic Ramayana

India's most expensive film - a lavish retelling of the Hindu epic Ramayana, made in two parts for a reported $500m (£370m) - has opened in cinemas worldwide, sparking enormous expectations and mixed reviews.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience.

One of Hinduism's foundational epics, the Ramayana has travelled across centuries and continents, finding expression in poetry, temple sculpture, shadow puppetry, folk theatre and stories passed down through generations. It has outlasted kingdoms and empires, inspired religious devotion and political movements, and found new life, again and again, on TV and in cinema.

Tiwari's version returns to the familiar story of love, duty, exile and war, set in a world of gods and demons, celestial weapons and mighty kingdoms.

Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Ram, the virtuous prince of Ayodhya. Banished from his kingdom for 14 years, he retreats to the forest with his wife Sita (played by Sai Pallavi), who is kidnapped by Ravana, the 10-headed king of Lanka.

Watch: Indian film star Ranbir Kapoor on AI, movies and fatherhood

Played by Yash, one of southern India's biggest stars, Ravana is a powerful warrior whose pride leads him into an epic battle with Ram (which will be depicted in part 2, set to release next year).

The film's producer, Namit Malhotra, heads visual-effects company DNEG , which has worked on Hollywood blockbusters including Dune and Interstellar. The music is a collaboration between AR Rahman, the Oscar-winning Indian composer of Slumdog Millionaire, and Hans Zimmer, whose scores for Gladiator, The Dark Knight and Dune have helped define the sound of modern Hollywood.

The film opened days ahead of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights which celebrates Ram's return to Ayodhya after his exile.

But the critical response so far has been mixed.

Saibal Chatterjee of NDTV channel gave it , external three out of five stars, saying its visual spectacle often overshadowed the story. Its enormous scale, he wrote, "remains, for the most part, the only thing that stands out", while the acting remains "wildly inconsistent".

The film's release comes days ahead of Diwali, which celebrates Ram's return to Ayodhya and the "victory of good over evil"

Rishabh Suri of the Hindustan Times newspaper was more enthusiastic, awarding it four stars.

"I am happy to report, all that money shows on screen," he wrote, praising the performances and visual effects, though he found the first half sluggish and the music underwhelming.

Shubhra Gupta , external of The Indian Express, who gave the film three stars, confessed to initial misgivings about its extravagant scale but found herself gradually won over, calling it the "perfect epic".

There was "enough sorcery and thrills and adventure" to sustain the spectacle, she wrote, and the filmmakers had managed to tell a sprawling story without being swallowed by it.

Internationally, too, the film drew contrasting reactions.

Writing in The Guardian, Peter Bradshaw called it a "thoroughly engaging, rousing and spectacular Indian epic melodrama". He found echoes of Shakespeare in the royal intrigue that sends Rama into exile, and of Homer in his quest to rescue Sita. Its sweeping landscapes and fantastical imagery reminded him of The Lord of the Rings and The Lion King.

"It's a rather amazing adventure," he wrote , external , giving it four stars.

Others were less impressed. Siddhant Adlakha of IGN scored the film four out of 10, describing its action as "clunky" and its computer-generated imagery as an "eye-sore".

Sita's abduction by Ravana sets off an epic battle

Giovanni Lago of Next Best Picture, who gave it , external five out of 10, praised Yash's magnetic Ravana and the score by Rahman and Zimmer. But he felt the film's vast narrative might have been better served by a Game of Thrones-style series.

The use of AI to adjust actors' lip movements for the English-language version also drew criticism. While Tiwari said it was intended to make the film more accessible to international audiences, Adlakha likened the result to "exaggerated mouth movements superimposed on still images for comedy sketches".

In India, the film has invited comparisons with earlier adaptations, particularly Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, which captivated the country nearly four decades ago with simple sets and special effects that now seem quaint.

When the series first aired in 1987, Sunday mornings across India took on an almost devotional stillness.

Streets emptied, shops lowered their shutters and neighbours crowded around TV sets. Some viewers bathed, lit incense and garlanded their screens before the broadcast, preparing for the show much as they might for worship.

Arvind Rajagopal, a media scholar at New York University, told the BBC in 2019 that trains and buses would stop and passengers disembark to watch the show on roadside TVs.

Broadcast on the state-run Doordarshan network, some of the most popular parts of the 78-episode series drew an estimated 80-100 million viewers, astonishing numbers at a time when owning a TV was a luxury in India.

The actors, too, became objects of reverence. Arun Govil, who played Ram, has recalled people weeping at the sight of him and touching his feet. Now, in a casting choice brimming with nostalgia, Govil returns in Tiwari's film as Dasharatha, Ram's father.

Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan remains the most popular adaptation of the Hindu epic to date

Other adaptations found their own ways to reimagine the epic. The 1992 Indo-Japanese animated film Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama brought the tale to life through richly detailed, hand-drawn animation.

Tiwari's Ramayana arrives with technological resources its predecessors could barely have imagined - but also with the expectations of generations who have grown up with the story and its characters.

It also comes at a politically charged moment in India, where Ram has become a powerful symbol of Hindu identity - over the past decade and a half, even popular analyses or retellings of the epic have landed in controversy.

The 2023 film Adipurush , another big-budget retelling of Ramayana, sparked backlash on several fronts.

Hindu groups called for a ban, accusing it of disrespecting religious figures, while some critics questioned its depiction of Ravana, which they said drew on Mughal imagery and reinforced stereotypes about Muslims. The film was also criticised for its dialogue and visual effects.

For the actors portraying these characters in the latest film, that burden was deeply felt.

"I was filled with fear," Kapoor told the BBC Asian Network's Haroon Rashid. "I knew that maybe I'm too old for this. I won't be able to do justice to it."

He called the role "an opportunity of a lifetime", but said playing a figure worshipped by millions left little room for the creative freedom he had enjoyed in other films.

Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, said the experience was as much spiritual as artistic. Raised in a religious household, she said she approached the part not just as a performance, but as an opportunity for personal growth.

How the film is being received will become clearer soon, as audiences head to cinemas.

But whatever the verdict, it marks a major cultural moment for India, bringing a story loved for generations to the big screen on an unprecedented scale.

Ibi byagarutsweho kuri uyu wa gatatu tariki 4 Ugushyingo ubwo Komisiyo y’Ubukungu n’Imari muri Sena yagezaga ku Nteko Rusange ya Sena raporo y’Umugenzuzi Mukuru w’Imari ya Leta y’umwaka w’ingengo y’imari warangiye ku wa 30 Kamena 2025.

Senateri Fulgence Nsengiyumva yavuze ko ikibazo cya WASAC gikwiye kwitabwaho by’umwihariko, kuko mu myaka itanu ishize yabonye "biragayitse" nk'uko bigaragara muri raporo y'Umugenzuzi Mukuru w’Imari ya Leta.

Ku rundi ruhande, raporo igaragaza ko amazi WASAC itabasha kwishyuza agera kuri 30%, bitewe n’imiyoboro ishaje, amazi yononekara ataragera ku bayakoresha.

Mu mwaka ushize, amazi WASAC itabashije kwishyuza abakiriya angana na 36% by’amazi yose yakwirakwije, ariko mu gihembwe cya mbere cy’uyu mwaka icyo gipimo cyaragabanutse kigera kuri 30%.

Bimwe mu bituma amazi apfa ubusa harimo imiyoboro ishaje, imiyoboro itabasha gutwara amazi ahagije, amatiyo ashaje ndetse n’ibura ry’abakozi.

Raporo y’Umugenzuzi Mukuru w’Imari ya Leta y’umwaka wa 2025 igaragaza ko WASAC yakoze metero kibe miliyoni 85,75 z’amazi, ariko ikabasha kwishyuza abakiriya metero kibe miliyoni 53,33 gusa, bingana na 62,2% by’amazi yose yakozwe.

Amazi atishyuwe yari afite agaciro ka miliyari 10,4 z’amafaranga y’u Rwanda, hakoreshejwe igiciro fatizo cya 323 Frw kuri metero kibe.

Nubwo igipimo cy’amazi apfa ubusa cyagabanutse, Abasenateri bagaragaje impungenge z’uko hari uduce tugikomeje kubura amazi.

Mu mishinga igamije kongera amazi harimo iya Nzove na Kanzenze, ndetse n’iteganyijwe mu rugomero rwa Nyabarongo ya Kabiri.

Mu bindi bibazo iyi Komisiyo yabonye bihuriweho n’inzego birimo imishinga y’abaterankunga isinywa ariko ikaba itaratangira gushyirwa mu bikorwa.

Ati “Byabonetse muri RTDA, RTPA, ariko byose twasanze biterwa no kudakora inyigo ku gihe turasanga inzego zibishinzwe zikwiye gufata ingamba”.

Ikindi yagarutseho ni amasezerano atinda gushyirwa mu bikorwa na ba rwiyemezamirimo agasaba ko inzego bireba ziba zikwiye kubikurikirana bigakorwa hakiri kare.

Ati “Ikindi kibazo twabonye n’ikijyanye n’Amafaranga yishyurwa mbere y’uko akazi gatangira(avance) zihabwa ba Rwiyemezamirimo kandi bataratangira imirimo”.

Ibindi bikubiye muri iyi Raporo ni agera kuri miliyoni 474 yasesaguwe, n’inzego zitandukanye zakorewe ubugenzuzu. Senateri Nsengiyumva ashimangira ko bidakwiye ko umutungo wa Leta ukoreshwa nabi kandi bishoboka kuwucunga neza.

Abasenateri bagaragaje kandi ibikwiye kwitabwaho birimo imishinga idindira, amasezerano y’imishinga adashyirwa mu bikorwa uko bikwiye , kutishyura abaturage ku gihe ingurane ku mitungo yabo, imitungo ya leta idakoreshwa, gutinda kugeza ku baturage serivisi z’ingenzi bakenera nk'amazi, amashanyarazi, imiti, ibikoresho byo kuhira imyaka, ibikoresho byo mu burezi, kudashyira mu bikorwa uko bikwiye inama z’ubugenzuzi.

Seanteri John Bideri Bond yavuze ko yizeye ko ibibazo birangwa mu nzego zitandukanye by’imicungire mibi y’imari ya Leta bizakemuka nk’uko umugenzuzi w’imari ya Leta Claudette Mukashyaka aherutse kubitangaza ubwo yinjiraga muri izi nshingano.

Perezida wa Sena, Dr. Kalinda François-Xavier, yavuze ko nyuma yo kugezwaho ibibazo bikubiye muri raporo ya Komisiyo y’Ubukungu n’Imari, Abasenateri bazabinyuza muri Komisiyo zitandukanye za Sena nazo zigasuzumira hamwe uko zizabigeza ku nzego bireba kugira ngo bishakirwe ibisubizo n’uburyo byakemuka.

MN202611_1wdaip12g3n.t:
43 players and eight members of staff received red cards after the brawl, as well as two board members

A world record of 53 red cards were shown during a chaotic under-20s game in Brazil.

The semi-final first leg of the Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship tie between Uberlandia and Mamore was marred by scenes that led to 43 players and eight members of coaching staff being sent off.

There was also two Uberlandia board members dismissed, taking the tally up to 53.

The previous record was 36, in a 2011 fifth-division game between Club Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in Argentina.

Brazilian news outlet O Tempo reported the military police were called , external because of extensive damage to the Parque do Sabia Stadium.

According to the referee's report, a brawl broke out in the second half after Mamores' Davi taunted the opposition bench during celebrations when his side went 3-1 up.

Uberlandia goalkeeping coach Paulo Sergio Dias Dos Santos ran on to the pitch to confront him, sparking clashes and the subsequent dismissals, with three players having already been sent off earlier.

The police report referenced 14 broken doors, damaged shower facilities, broken windows and that benches, tables and chairs had been destroyed.

The game was paused for approximately 40 minutes and then abandoned by referee Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto.

"In the 54th minute of the second ​half, a generalized brawl broke out, making it impossible to show the red cards and to carry ‌out the ⁠match-closing protocol," Modesto wrote in his report.

"Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared the match ended."

Uberlandia have since confirmed , external that they have conceded the second leg of the semi-final because Mamore only have seven players available as a result of all the red cards.

They described their move as a "gesture of fair play" as Mamore would progress through to the final, and Uberlandia will instead focus on the third-place match.

"The club has also not remained silent: ​the appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally, because athletic development is, above all, a ​matter of personal development," Uberlandia added.

MN202611_86lbvke8ce.t:
Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has met the US-based owners of Poundland as the government hopes to save the retailer from collapse.

The discount chain is on the brink of insolvency and Gordon Brothers, which bought it for £1 last June, has rejected a takeover bid which could have saved the 12,000 jobs currently at risk.

A meeting was due to be held on Thursday but was brought forward as the scramble to secure a rescue deal for the firm intensifies.

Gordon Brothers said it is "pursuing all avenues through the sales process" but that Poundland has faced several years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable".

The firm said it is "engaging in active discussions on offers with interested parties".

It added: "When Gordon Brothers acquired the business, it was in distress and required a radical restructure, urgent operational change and significant funding, which we provided to support the company's ability to trade."

Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of the business has not been made.

On Wednesday, a source close to business secretary said Reynolds "has been firm that Gordon Brothers must do everything in their power to protect jobs and provide certainty for workers".

"He is pleased to have secured this commitment from Gordon Brothers in the meeting and will continue to hold the company to account and closely monitor developments," the source added.

It is understood that Gordon Brothers made a commitment in the meeting to prioritise bids that will protect workers and units.

However, it is still unclear whether the US investment firm will keep the business together or break it up.

Meanwhile, MPs say they have called in Poundland's owners for questioning on Wednesday 11 November to explain their role in the discount retailer's looming insolvency.

Liam Byrne, chair of Parliament's business committee, said: "Every report suggests Poundland is a viable, profitable business with a future ahead of it and without good reason to let it crash and burn - and then to break it up and sell it off piece by piece.

"We are asking Gordon Brothers to appear before Parliament to explain themselves and tell us just what it is that's preventing them from accepting the fully-funded deal on the table to save more than 12,000 jobs."

Business Minister Kate Dearden and union representatives met Poundland's managing director Barry Williams on Wednesday.

Mr Williams told the BBC that Poundland is profitable and sales were growing.

"We're back in profit and it has a bright future ahead of it if it's allowed to deliver that," he said.

Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until next Thursday.

Adam Turner: We would lose "a few million" if Poundland went under

Asked what his message for Poundland's owner was, Burnham said Gordon Brothers should "focus on the people in your employment" and "come up with a practical solution that saves jobs and saves those stores".

"There is a solution to be found here, sit down with us and let's find it," he added.

The meeting comes after a major Poundland supplier has said it will lose millions of pounds if the retailer goes bust.

Adam Turner, sales director at Bradford-based Highcrest Retail Brands, said Poundland was one of its biggest customers and its collapse would cost it "a few million" in lost sales.

The family owned business mainly sells confectionery to Poundland and turns over about £50m.

Turner said the firm becoming insolvent would leave a substantial gap in its balance sheet next year.

Highcrest was a "longstanding business that can stomach this", Turner said. But he warned other medium and small suppliers to the retailer have told him that "if Poundland goes under, so do they".

This echoes a warning from Poundland founder Steve Smith on Monday that two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, which only work for Poundland, would be directly affected by its collapse.

Not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall, he told the BBC on Wednesday.

He said he was "amazed" Poundland was being put into administration, pointing to the profitability of the company.

"Also, there's two offers on the table from some really good people," he added.

"All I'm asking is for Gordon Brothers to see if they can put a deal together."

Gordon Brothers said Walsall-based Poundland is "still not cash generative at a sustainable level" because of the economic issues it faces.

If Poundland's stores are sold to new buyers, some of the employees may get new jobs on the same premises.

However, it is understood that buyers are only interested in about half the stores at present – meaning roughly 6,000 employees would not be re-employed.

Poundland's founder offers to invest in firm

If Poundland goes under, suppliers will be getting "pennies in the pound" back from the administration, he said, which is "very upsetting" – although he still hopes a deal can be done so Poundland can remain solvent.

Poundland owners Gordon Brothers will be a secured creditor, which means they are first in line to get their money back, and suppliers "who have done nothing wrong" will take the financial hit.

"It's sad. It's a nightmare for us all to be honest with you. It's not just the suppliers, it's the staff at Poundland, some of these guys have been there for many years.

"It's from the warehouse staff all the way to the shop staff to everybody within head office. It's a massive ripple effect through the supply chain," he added.

Turner said he had no knowledge of whether Gordon Brothers had deliberately timed the process of Poundland going into administration so it could take advantage of having high stock levels, which it can then sell.

One of the ways Gordon Brothers makes money is through stock liquidations – selling off stock from collapsed businesses.

One insider familiar with the situation told the BBC that the timing of Poundland facing collapse was "odd" – most retailers don't fall over in the run-up to Christmas.

Dearden has said the government doesn't want to interfere with "current ongoing commercial negotiations", but that ministers want "clarity" on the plans for the retailer.

"It's absolutely legitimate for this government to ask the business if they're doing everything they can to protect employees and suppliers up and down the country," she added.

Dearden told MPs that the government would be ready to help the company's employees if Poundland collapses.

The head of Gordon Brothers' European operations reportedly told the government that the firm stood by its stewardship and had given Poundland £85m in additional financing since its purchase in 2025.

Ambasaderi w’u Rwanda muri Sénégal, Festus Bizimana, yakurikiye amarushanwa yo koga mu Mikino Olempike y’Urubyiruko ya 2026 iri kubera i Dakar, aho abakinnyi bane b’Abanyarwanda bahagarariye Igihugu muri iri rushanwa. Abo bakinnyi ni Mugabo Aragsan Liban, Ntwali Jayden, Keza Kalisa na Murenzi Sheja Kean. Ambasaderi Bizimana yabashimiye umuhate, ubutwari n’umwuka wo guhatana bagaragaje bahagarariye u Rwanda kuri uru rwego mpuzamahanga.

Yavuze ko kwitabira iyi mikino ari amahirwe akomeye ku rubyiruko, kuko bibafasha guhangana n’abandi bakinnyi bakiri bato beza ku Isi, kunguka ubunararibonye no kurushaho kuzamura urwego rwabo.

Ambasaderi Bizimana yashishikarije abakinnyi gukomeza kwigirira icyizere, gushyiramo imbaraga no gukoresha neza aya mahirwe, abizeza ko igihugu kibari inyuma kandi kizakomeza kubatera ingabo mu bitugu mu gihe cy’amarushanwa.

Yagize ati: “Turi inyuma yanyu kandi tuzakomeza kubatera inkunga mu gihe cyose amarushanwa azamara.”

Mugabo Aragsan ni we washyizeho agahigo gashya mu Rwanda mu cyiciro cya metero 50 mu koga mu buryo bwa Freestyle, aho yakoresheje amasegonda 29.94.

Ntwali Jayden na we yitwaye neza, agira ibihe bibiri bishya byiza kurusha ibyo yari asanzwe afite. Yakoze amasegonda 27.15 muri metero 50 za Freestyle, avuye ku masegonda 27.41, ndetse akora amasegonda 28.66 muri metero 50 za Butterfly, avuye ku masegonda 29.12.

Kalisa Keza na we yanditse amateka ye bwite, akora amasegonda 36.11 muri metero 50 za Butterfly, bikaba ari ibihe byiza kurusha ibyo yari asanzwe afite.

Imikino Olempike y’Urubyiruko ya Dakar 2026 yatangiye ku wa 31 Ukwakira 2026, mu muhango wo kuyitangiza ku mugaragaro wabereye kuri Stade Abdoulaye Wade i Diamniadio, muri Sénégal.

MN202611_4srf98kbq2.t:
Roger Johnson called on his colleagues to unite for Children in Need

I'm not much of a runner. I never have been.

But I have been getting my trainers on most mornings for the past 18 months, simply to stay fit and lose weight.

So, I wasn't too daunted when I was challenged to run 26.2 miles (41km) over the space of two weeks for this year's BBC Children in Need appeal.

Lots of people do a marathon in one go, so how hard could it be?

Well, perhaps I shouldn't have been so conceited.

Four weeks ago, a long-standing foot problem flared up.

I iced it. I raised it. The doctor gave me pills. I even had an X-ray.

But it stubbornly refused to get better.

It was a team effort to complete the Children in Need challenge

Members of Lostock Athletics Club had kindly offered to run the first few miles with me, and it was arranged for a drizzly Tuesday morning in Blackrod, near Horwich.

I arrived, hobbling, and had to watch bemused as they jogged off into the distance without me.

Ian Burns, who is in his late 60s, offered some words of wisdom.

"We are a bit stubborn and think we're not really hurt when we really are," he said.

"It can take me weeks to get over a small injury, whereas 10 years ago, I would have been a couple of days."

Supporting over 2,600 projects, working 365 days a year, all over the United Kingdom. Get involved to help make a difference to children and young people on your doorstep.

Either way, I hoped I would soon be fit to start the challenge.

I waited and waited. It felt as though I was taking painkillers like sweets (while never exceeding the recommended dose, of course).

But by the end of October, still unable to manage more than a hobble, I needed a Plan B.

And that was when, as I looked around the BBC North West newsroom, I realised salvation could be close at hand.

Could a few colleagues join forces to run the miles on my behalf?

More than 30 people ran more 160 miles between them

The essence of Children in Need, since it started in 1980, has been about strangers coming together to raise money to help others.

Over the decades, I've met so many fundraisers and those they help.

I've heard stories which have made me laugh and cry.

I will always remember an elderly lady in Bootle, Merseyside, who had just collected her pension and insisted on putting £20 in a collection bucket as we walked down the north west coast.

And Ella, supported by a bereavement charity on the Isle of Man, after her brother died.

Colleagues put their best foot forward to complete the challenge

Generosity runs through it all - money, of course, but also generosity of time and spirit.

So maybe I shouldn't have been surprised when my colleagues started replying to my email.

In the end, more than 30 ran more 160 miles between them in parks, on paths, up and down hills, over bridges and along the lanes of Cheshire, Lancashire, Greater Manchester, Merseyside and Cumbria.

That figure was far more than my target, but it stands for the power of the collective uniting for a common cause.

It's what Children in Need is all about.

But it's also taught me another lesson - if I'm asked again to do something for the cause next year, I will promise to be a little less complacent.

BBC Children in Need 2026 will be live on BBC iPlayer and BBC One from 19:00 GMT on 13 November.

MN202611_14odocp6ktj.t:
The Dark Knight starred Christian Bale and Heath Ledger

A motorcycle used in Sir Christopher Nolan's Oscar-winning 2008 Batman film The Dark Knight is expected to sell for up to £900,000 at auction.

The vehicle is among lots being sold by Hertfordshire-based Propstore online and at Bafta in London from 4 -6 December.

The "Batpod" was featured in a chase scene that included Christian Bale's Batman and Heath Ledger's Joker and it also appeared in the 2012 sequel The Dark Knight Rises.

The prop is predicted to sell for between £450,000 and £900,000.

The Dark Knight was filmed on location in Chicago and Hong Kong, while large indoor sets were built at the airship hangars in Cardington, Bedfordshire.

Bale's complete Batsuit from Batman Begins, the first film in the trilogy, is also for sale, with an estimate of between £125,000 and £250,000.

Propstore founder Stephen Lane described the bike as an "extraordinary feat of filmmaking and engineering"

Items from Indiana Jones's costume in Temple of Doom, including the protagonist's fedora, are being sold at the same auction.

The items came from the collection of stuntman Vic Armstrong, who doubled for Harrison Ford in the first three Indiana Jones films, which were shot at Elstree Studios in Hertfordshire.

They join other items from Game Of Thrones, Superman III and Conan The Barbarian.

Costumes and a whip from the second Indiana Jones movie are also being sold during the auction

Stephen Lane, the founder and CEO of Propstore, described the Batman vehicle as an "extraordinary feat of filmmaking and engineering".

He added: "Bringing together Indiana Jones' fedora, shirt and bullwhip in the same catalog is particularly exciting.

"With the fedora and shirt coming directly from legendary stunt performer Vic Armstrong's personal collection, they also tell the story of the remarkable stunt work behind the adventure."

MN202611_cltwnnmt4h.t:
Paul Elliott will star as Mr Boo in the The Rise and Fall of Little Voice

They say it's never too late to try something new and, after more than six decades in the entertainment industry, Paul Chuckle is about to prove that true.

Real name Paul Elliott, the 79-year-old, is preparing to appear in his first ever play, taking on the role of Mr Boo in Jim Carwright's The Rise and Fall of Little Voice at the National Theatre.

Elliott, from Rotherham, became a household name, alongside his late brother Barry, as one half of the haphazard Chuckle Brothers in children's TV show ChuckleVision, which ran from 1987 to 2009.

But now, after decades of playing for laughs, he is just weeks away from what he has described as his first ever "straight play".

Speaking to the BBC, he said: "63 years in the business and it's my first ever play, and, would you believe it, it's at the National Theatre - you can't write it.

"A young lad from East Herringthorpe, and now at the National.

Following the death of his brother in 2018 , Elliott said he was determined not to retire, and, in recent years, has turned his hand to a variety of new opportunities.

In 2025 he starred in a gangster movie, playing The Jackal in Fall to the Top, and later the same year appeared in Celebrity MasterChef.

In keeping with trying new things, he is also set to star as Monsignor O'Hara in a touring production of Sister Act at the end of 2027.

Paul and Barry Elliott starred together as the Chuckle Brothers on stage and TV

The Rise and Fall of Little Voice tells the story of as a shy girl who rarely ventures outside her bedroom, until her talent for imitating famous singers is recognised by a local promoter.

Elliott will perform alongside Silent Witness actress Francesca Mills, who will play the title role, and Waterloo Road star Jill Halfpenny, who will play her mother, Mari Hoff.

After a career including, TV, film, pantomime, circus and now regular DJ sets, he said adapting had been a challenge.

"It's the first show I've done in many, many years without saying 'to me, to you'.

"The lines are slowly sinking into my brain.

"I've found that hard. Barry and I ad libbed a lot when we were on stage.

"We had lots of fun, we used to fall about laughing at each other, but there's none of that, I've got to be word perfect.

"TV is easier. If you go wrong it's 'cut, do it again' but on stage you can't.

"When me and Barry worked together we loved things going wrong, but you can't do that in a live play."

One thing Elliott said he did know well ahead of stepping into the shoes of club promoter Mr Boo was the world of working men's clubs.

"Jim Cartwright, who wrote the play, he thought I would be perfect for the part of Mr Boo," he said.

"I was working in working men's clubs all my career, and he knew I was doing that.

"We did all the clubs in the North East, South Wales, Midlands, North Wales, wherever we could get the work, we grew up in working men's clubs. Not an easy life, may I tell you. Not an easy life.

"You never knew whether they're going to love you or hate you, and there was no real middle ground.

"They were either a fabulous audience or a terrible audience, or put it the other way, we were terrible or brilliant."

The Rise and Fall of Little Voice, directed by Robert Hastie, will run at the National Theatre in London from 2 December to 23 January, before heading to locations including Newcastle, Sheffield and Salford.
